PREFACE
 
          I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource
Development, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this
Hundred-Sixty Ninth Report on Action Taken by the Government on the recommendations contained in its Hundred
Sixty Third Report onDemands for Grants (Demand No.105) of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports for the year
2005-2006.
2.         The Hundred Sixty Third Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human
Resource Development was presented to the Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on 6
th May, 2005. 
Replies of the Government on the recommendations contained in the Report received from the Ministry of Youth
Affairs and Sports were considered by the Committee at its meeting held on the 8th December, 2005.

 CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH  HAVE  BEEN ACCEPTED BY GOVERNMENT
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
II.        NATIONAL YOUTH POLICY, 2003
 
Para 2.1          In order to fulfil the legitimate aspirations and to empower the youth in the age group of 13-35 years to
successfully accomplish the challenging tasks of national reconstruction and social change that lie ahead, the National
Youth Policy has been launched which envisages that all Ministries/Departments of the Central and State Governments
particularly, in the social sectors will strive to make identifiable allocations in their budget for youth development
programmes.  The Committee welcomes the idea of making identifiable allocation for youth programmes by not only
the Central Ministries/Departments but by States also.  This would provide a clear picture about the efforts and
resources devoted for this purpose.  Such youth specific allocations be shown by all the Ministries/Departments from
the year 2006-07 itself.

ACTION TAKEN
The provision made in the “Implementation Mechanism” of the National Youth Policy, 2003 that “all
Ministries/Departments of the Union Government and the State Governments, particularly in the social sector will strive
to make identifiable allocation in their budget for youth Development Programmes” has already been brought to their
notice.  However, concerned Union Ministries/Departments are being asked separately to make youth specific
allocations in their budget commencing from the financial year 2006-07.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
III.       NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR YOUTH
 
Para 3.1          The National Commission for Youth (NCY), which was set up in March, 2002 adopted its report in its
meeting held on 5
th July, 2004 and submitted the same to the Ministry on 17 th July, 2004.  The report of the
Commission was laid on the Table of both Houses of Parliament on 23 rd December, 2004.  A number of
recommendations have been made by the Commission out of which 14 recommendations have been accepted in
principle by the Ministry.  The Committee would like to be apprised about the recommendations of the Commission that
have been accepted for implementation.  The Committee hopes that youth – the future leaders of the country could be
made instrumental towards achieving socio-economic changes and technological excellence and thus contribute towards
national development.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The status of the implementation of the recommendations of the National Commission for Youth has been
indicated in Annexure-I.
 
IV.       BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 4.1          Total outlay, both Plan and Non-Plan taken together provided to the Ministry for the year 2004-05, was
Rs. 466.00 crores.  It was decreased to Rs. 441.00 crores in RE 2004-05.  The budget allocation for 2005-06 is Rs.
506.99 crores (Plan Rs. 438.99 crores and Non Plan Rs. 68.00 crores) against a projected demand of Rs. 691.00 crores
(Rs. 610.27 crores under Plan and Rs. 80.81 crores under Non-Plan).  The Plan projections, the Committee was
informed, were made in view of the requirements of the Commonwealth Games, 2010 and proposal for extending the
National Service Scheme to all schools in the country in accordance with the commitment made in the Common
Minimum Programmes of the Government.  The Committee feels that the Ministry’s projection for the annual plan,
2005-06 was quite justified because it constituted only 10% increase over the previous year’s allocations and also
because the Ministry has to fulfil its obligation for the preparations of the Commonwealth Games, 2010 and expansion
of NSS up to the school level.  There appears to be no justification in applying cut to its allocations, particularly when
the Ministry was able to spend more than 66.72% of its allocation up to December, 2004, as per the existing norms in
this regard.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The Ministry is grateful to the Hon’ble Committee for its support.
 
V.        NEHRU YUVA KENDRA SANGATHAN
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 5.10         The Committee also suggests that Department should make every possible efforts to clear the
confusion/uncertainties in respect of recruitment test that was held for selecting Youth Coordinators.

ACTION TAKEN
 
The matter is sub-judice.
 
VIII.    RASHTRIYA SADBHAWANA YOJNA
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 8.4           The Committee notes that this scheme has taken the place of erstwhile National Reconstruction Corps
Scheme, which continued upto March, 2003.  It has taken two years in formulation of the revised scheme.  The
Committee hopes that this scheme would not suffer from the shortcomings experienced in the implementation of the
earlier scheme.
 
ACTION TAKEN
Since the scheme has been implemented w.e.f. 01.04.2005, a review of the scheme will be made after it
completes one year.  The observations of the Committee have been communicated to the Nehru Yuva Kendra
Sangathan, which is the implementing agency for Rashtriya Sadbhavana Yojana. As regards efficacy of 10-20 Sathees
in a district as well as  honorarium of Rs. 1000/-, the matter will be taken up during Mid Term review of the scheme
before 11
th Five Year Plan.
            While formulating the scheme, the shortcomings experienced in the implementation of the old scheme has been
taken in view.  Since volunteers are selected by the Clubs from amongst its own members, there would be transparency
in the selection process. 
 
IX.       SCHEME OF PROMOTION OF NATIONAL INTEGRATION
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 9.5          The Committee notes that the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai was being asked to conduct an
assessment about the impact of the work done by various voluntary agencies under the Scheme of Promotion of
National Integration.  The Madras School of Social Work, Chennai also is being asked to undertake the study on Inter-
State Youth Exchange Programme.  The Committee recommends that the institutions assigned the job of the assessment
should be asked to adhere to a time frame in submitting their reports.  The Committee would also like to be apprised of
the outcome of the assessment along-with the action taken by the Ministry thereon.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
Recommendations of the Committee are noted for future guidance.       
 
XI.       FINACIAL ASSISTANCE TO RURAL YOUTH CLUBS/SPORTS CLUBS
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 11.3        An allocation of Rs. 6.75 crores under the Scheme has been provided in BE 2005-06 against an
allocation of Rs. 3.15 crores BE and RE Rs. 5.35 crores in the year 2004-05.  The Committee is not sure whether last
year’s budget could be fully utilized under the scheme.  It was Rs. 2.83 crores upto 28
th February, 2005.  The enhanced
allocation would include additional grants to Youth Clubs, YDCs, as it is the thrust area identified by Cabinet
Secretariat.  500 RITYDCs and 500 YDCs are proposed to be set up during the current plan period.  The Committee
notes that allocation for this scheme has been nearly doubled in 2005-06 and hopes that entire amount would be utilized
for achieving targets of setting up 500 each YDCs and RITYDCs.  The Committee recommends that the proposed
RITYDCs and YDCs should be proportionately distributed so as to cover all the regions of the country.
 
ACTION TAKEN

Recommendation of the Committee is noted for compliance.                 
 
XII.     PROMOTION OF YOUTH ACTIVITIES AND TRAINING
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 12.3         The Committee notes that vocational training is one of the components of the scheme.  In view of the
number of youth being unemployed due to diminishing job opportunities, it is advisable that more and more vocational
training programmes aimed towards gainful employment be designed.  These training programmes would go a long way
in channelising the hidden potential and energies of the youth towards constructivework.  And at the same time, itwould
also prevent migration of rural youth to cities where they are forced to live a sub-human life apart from falling victims
of anti-social elements.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
Noted for future compliance.                
 
XVII.   SPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 17.4        The Committee notes that the BE allocation of Rs. 123.83 crores was reduced at RE to 117.75 crores in
2004-05.  The actual expenditure reported upto 28.3.2005 was Rs. 85.61 crores only.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The revised Budget Estimate of Rs.117.75 crores, allocated for the year 2004-05 was utilized by 31.3.2005.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
17.5     The Committee would like to remind the Ministry about its last years observations on the issue of under
utilization of funds.  The Ministry in its action taken note has informed that SAI has been instructed to ensure the
optimum utilization of funds under its various Plan Schemes.  Unfortunately the status of utilization does not show any
improvement in 2004-05 either.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates its earlier recommendation and would like the
Ministry to adopt stringent fiscal measures and guidelines for streamlining its funding pattern.  SAI should be asked by
the Ministry to strictly adhere to those guidelines in utilizing allocations appropriately.
 
ACTION TAKEN
The utilization of the revised budgetary allocation (reduction due to cut of Rs. 25.00 crore by Finance) of Rs.
117.75 crore has been fully utilized by SAI.
ALL INDIA COUNCIL OF PHYSICAL EDUCATION
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 25.1        The decision to set-up an All India Council for Physical Education was taken in May, 1994 in a meeting
of major Physical Education Associations of the country, held under the Chairmanship of the then Minister of Youth
Affairs & Sports. The Committee observed that the decision remained unimplemented for almost ten years. The
Committee finds that during the Ninth Plan, a token provision of Rs.4.00 lakh was kept for this Council. This token
provision has been enhanced to Rs. 93.00 lakhs in the Tenth Plan period. However, the position remains unchanged with
a token amount being provided every year without a single rupee being spent. In   March, 2004 it was decided after
going through the comments/observations of various concerned Ministries/Department/Organizations not to set up such
a Council. Reason given for it was that another statutory body i.e. National Council of Teacher Education has already
laid down regulations on Physical Education. The Committee is surprised to note that a final decision is yet to be taken
as the matter still remains under consideration in consultation with the Ministry of HRD. The Committee fails to

understand the constraints in taking a decision on this issue of setting or not setting up of the All India Council of
Physical Education.  The Committee strongly feels that this issue must be settled at the earliest.
 
ACTION TAKEN
It has been decided to drop the proposal for setting up the All India Council of Physical Education (AICPE) in
view of the fact that a Statutory Body already exists to regulate this aspect of the Education.
CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH  THE COMMITEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN
VIEW OF GOVERNMENTS REPLY
 
IV.
              BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 4.2          The Committee was informed that allocation made to the Ministry in 2005-06, constituted just 0.98 per
cent of the entire Budget of the Government of India.  The Committee considers it disappointingly low in view of the
mandate of the Ministry being to develop the personality of our youth as also involving them in nation-building
activities.  This group, which constitutes nearly 40 per cent of total population of India, is the most vibrant and potent
segment of our society.  Allocation below one percent to youth development and sports reflects a low preference.  The
Committee is of the considered opinion that there is a strong case of adequate allocation for the Ministry in the coming
years.  Department’s demand for a share in the funds collected through education cess must be considered favourably,
particularly for expansion of NSS up to 9
th class and also in all the remaining schools.
 
ACTION TAKEN
            The matter has been being taken up with Planning Commission for the Ministry’s share in the funds collected
through education cess.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 4.4          Even during the Ninth Plan, funds remained underutilized in different categories.  For example, of the
total Ninth Plan outlay of Rs. 352.24 crores for Youth Welfare, only Rs. 336.94 crores could be spent.  The schemes
suffering most were: National Reconstruction Corps, Youth Hostels and Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth
Development.  Similarly, spending Rs. 558.50 crores in Ninth Plan period against an outlay of Rs. 472.61 under Sports
and Physical Education also indicates towards fiscal (mal) practices such as unspent balances or re-appropriation etc. 
The Committee is of the view that these situations- under-utilization as well as unspent balances – indicate that both our
delivery mechanism as well as system of flow of funds are not foolproof and need to be streamlined further.  It reflects a
poor physical performance because it is directly related to the financial performance.
 
ACTION TAKEN
Effective steps for systematic flow of expenditure (quarter-wise) have been taken in recent past.  The position
regarding specific schemes mentioned above is as follows:
 
NRC Scheme has been revamped w.e.f. 31.3.2003 and new scheme under the name of Rashtriya Sadbhavana
Yojana has since been launched this year.  The competition among Youth Clubs has been completed and the selection of
volunteers by the best youth clubs has been finalized.  The enrolled volunteers are being given training to act as
facilitators for the youth clubs in their respective areas.
 
The main reason for non-utilisation of budgeted outlay was non-receipt of utilization certificates of grants
already released and further progress reports from the concerned State Governments.  The matter for expediting the
construction of hostels was taken up by Secretary, YAS with Chief Secretaries of all the concerned States on 17.2.05. 
This has resulted in completion of 4 youth hostel projects and receipt of progress reports of 10 more hostels being
constructed at various places. A total of Rs. 198.13 lakh has been released during the period March, 2005 to July, 2005
as per Annexure - II.  We have committed liability of Rs.14.09 crores, as on 17.8.05, for the 22 on-going youth hostels

under construction and as all the projects are being monitored regularly, it is felt that not only the allocated budget for
the scheme will be fully utilized, we will require additional funds at RE Stage also for release to the concerned State
Governments.
 
As far as RGNIYD is concerned, till 2004-05 only two faculty posts had been sanctioned and the infrastructure
had remained incomplete.  During 2004-05, a number of initiatives have been taken to strengthen and streamline the
working of the institute.  These include creation of five Academic Divisions; networking with Universities through IT;
construction projects in the campus have been completed and construction work of the Auditorium has commenced.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 4.5          While appreciating the formulation of quarterly Action Plans during Tenth Plan by the Ministry, the
Committee feels that it has not been able to achieve the desired results.  The Committee would like to emphasize the
need for the judicious and optimum utilization of funds by the Ministry allocated for various schemes.
 
ACTION TAKEN
Noted for guidance.  During 2004-05, the Ministry took number of steps to ensure the physical performance
under various schemes with a view to achieve the desired results.  The physical targets achieved during 2004-05 under
various Schemes is indicated at Annexure- III.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 4.6          The Committee is of the view that a detailed review of the schemes showing poor performance should be
undertaken so as to identify the shortcomings and initiate remedial measures.  The Ministry should involve the Planning
Commission, the State Governments and other implementing agencies in this exercise.
 
ACTION TAKEN
The following initiatives have been undertaken in this regard:
            On Youth side, the Scheme of NRC which was implemented on a pilot basis has been reviewed and a new
scheme, i.e. Rashtriya Sadbhavana Yojana, has been launched from 01.04.2005.
            The financial norms of the various schemes being implemented by Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan have been
revised with effect from 01.04.2005.  A number of initiatives, including new MIS System, have been introduced to
strengthen and streamline the implementation of these schemes.
 
            In National Service Scheme, a review of the Scheme has been undertaken during 2004-05 and proposal for its
deepening and expanding the scheme has been forwarded to the Planning Commission for its in-principle approval.
 
            On Sports side, the review has been undertaken.  A fresh Scheme “Sports for Disabled” is being formulated. 
The Schemes of State Sports Academy and Assistance to National Sports Federations have been identified for revision. 
Wide ranging discussion has been held.  Planning Commission, State Governments, Corporate Sector and eminent
sportspersons have been consulted.  The revised Scheme has been formulated and is being processed for Expenditure
Finance Committee’s approval.  A new initiative i.e. Champion Promotion has been launched to facilitate National
Champions for achieving excellence in Sports.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
                       
Para 4.7          The Committee is aware of the structural problems inherent in our system from Union level down to the
Panchayats in implementing the central sector as well as centrally-sponsored schemes.  Ours being basically a
cooperative federation, States have got to play a more pro-active and coordinated role in this exercise for obtaining the
desired impact of the schemes at the ground level.
 
ACTION TAKEN
The Ministry held a meeting of Sports and Youth Affairs Ministers to highlight the need of proactive role of
States.  The State Governments and District Administrations are being involved in monitoring of various youth sector

Schemes, like NSS, youth hostels, funding to NGOs as well as schemes being implemented by Nehru Yuva Kendra
Sangathan.  Volunteers of youth clubs are being encouraged to actively participate in the Gram Sabha meetings.  The
assisted youth clubs having been recognized as NGOs are taking up, projects for the Community development in their
respective areas.  On sports side, the states are actively involved in Schemes of Talent Search, State Training Centres
and Special Area Games and State Coaching Centres as well as Scholarship to Sportspersons.  The State Sports
Academy can also be implemented through the State Governments.
 
V.        NEHRU YUVA KENDRA SANGATHAN (NYKS)
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 5.2          A new initiative entitled Gandhi Gramodaya Sankalp Abhiyan – Model Village Project was launched in
2004 under which NY Kendra will adopt one village with a view to develop it as a model self-reliant village.  497 NYK
Districts have been identified for developing self-reliant villages on the principles of Gram Swaraj as propagated by
Mahatma Gandhi.  A new scheme entitled Rashtriya Sadbhavana Yojna has been approved for empowering rural youth
clubs and promoting leadership among them.  The Committee feels that adequate publicity should be given to all youth
programmes, particularly this new scheme, through print and electronic media.
 
ACTION TAKEN
The Schemes of MYAS are being given due publicity by NYKS during all its youth clubs meetings, training
programmes.  Since 2004-05, a newsletter is being regularly published by NYKS. The schemes are also publicized
through the official web site of MYAS.  As far as Rashtriya Sadhbhavana Yojana is concerned, the process for the
selection of Nehru Yuva Sathees under the scheme has been completed.  The training of volunteers is under way. The
selection process itself has given lot of publicity to the scheme.  Since, NYKS is implementing a large number of
schemes of this and other Ministries, this process also enables it to provide publicity to its schemes
.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 5.5          The Committee is of the view that in order to fulfil its social responsibility, the Youth Clubs and Mahila
Mandals should be encouraged to work as watchdog agencies against drug and human trafficking, HIV/AIDs etc.  They
need to be encouraged to actively participate in awareness generation and promoting activities relating to national
integration.
 
ACTION TAKEN
Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan is one of the agencies actively engaged in programmes working for the
prevention of HIV-AIDS, Drug Abuse and Human trafficking. Nehru Yuva Kendras’ affiliated Youth Clubs regularly
organize various programmes in connection with these issues.  International Day of Drug Abuse and Human
Trafficking, World AIDS Day etc. are observed by NYK regularly.  NYKS had earlier implementing schemes like
Villagers Talk AIDS programmes with the cooperation of National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO).  Now NYKS
has undertaken implementation of Red Ribbon Express project in collaboration with NACO and Rajiv Gandhi
Foundation (RGF). The participants as well as beneficiaries of the project include all Youth Club and Mahila Mandal
members.  Recently, all the senior level officers of NYKS have been trained in Drug Abuse Prevention activities with
the help of National Institute of Social Defence under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
 
The Youth Clubs and Mahila Mandals affiliated to NYKS are working for the promotion of National Integration
and Communal Harmony. Youth Club members are also participants of the National Integration Camps organized by
NYKS and the Ministry.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 5.7          While appreciating the idea of utilizing the services of the NYKS by other Ministries/Departments for
improving the outreach of their programmes, the Committee has a word of caution in this regard.  The basic mandate of
the NY Kendras should not get diluted/ignored, the possibility of which cannot be ruled out in this situation.  The
Committee feels that a well-coordinated monitoring mechanism would be required, if NY Kendras were to participate in

169th Report of Committee on Human Resourse Development
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/169threport.htm[01-07-2016 15:24:39]
schemes run by eight to nine Ministries/agencies.
 
In view of the 97 vacant posts of District Youth Coordinators, the Committee expresses its reservations about an
effective implementation of such programmes in addition to the programmes being run by NYKS at present.  Moreover,
nearly 100 districts are yet to have NY Kendras in the country.  The Committee recommends that all the existing
District Kendras should be equipped with requisite infrastructure and manpower for handling such a large number of
programmes.  Committee would like to be apprised of details of various State level programmes being undertaken by
NYKS.  The Committee has been given to understand that state govts. have been asked to converge their programmes
with NYKS.  The Committee feels that this is the right initiative taken by the Ministry.  The Committee is of theview
that a study can be initiated by the Ministry whereunder State and Centre-run programmes could be analysed and
element of overlapping if any, in schemes may be eliminated.
 
ACTION TAKEN
The Committee’s observation on the mandate of NYKS is noted.
 
A list of the State level programmes being undertaken by NYKS is at Annexure- V.  The Committee’s
suggestion about a study to be initiated by the Ministry would be taken up.
 
VI.       NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME (NSS)
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATIONS
 
Para 6.3          The Committee is happy to note that the physical and financial performance of the NSS during 2002-03,
2003-04 and 2004-05 have been satisfactory.  It, however, needs to be still improved, specially, the trend of utilization
in 2004-05.  Although BE allocation of Rs. 28.00 crore was enhanced to Rs. 33.50 crore, actual expenditure figures upto
28.2.05 is only Rs. 23.25 crores, which was even less than the BE provision.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
It is submitted that the total expenditure finally for the year 2004-05 was 100% i.e Rs.33.04 crore.  The

PREFACE

I, the Chairman of the Department related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Human Resource Development, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Seventeenth Report of the Committee on the
Demands for Grants (Demand No. 47) of the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports,
Ministry of Human Resource Development for the Year 1995-96.

2. The Committee considered the various documents and relevant papers received from
the Deptt. of Youth Affairs & Sports Ministry of Human Resource Development and also
heard the Secretary and other Officials of that Deptt. on the said Demands for Grants in its
meeting held on 29th March, 1995.

3. The Committee considered the Draft Report and adopted the same on 17th April,
1995.

New Devut; P. UPENDRA,
April 17, 1995 Chairman,
Ss Department-related Parliamentary
27, Chaitra, 1917 (Saka) Standing Committee on

Human Resource Development.


REPORT

The Department of Youth Affairs and Sports is one of the four constituent Departments
of the Ministry of Human Resource Development. The Department has taken a number of
new initiatives and programmes in the field of youth development and sports, as well as
physical education. The Programme undertaken by the Department can be broadly classified
under (I) Youth Programmes and (II) Sports and Games.

Youth Programmes

2. The Department finances various youth welfare programmes, which range from
personality development to vocational training. Most of these programmes are itnplemented
by reputed institutions. NGOs, as well as State Governments for which financial assistance is
provided by this Department as per stipulated norms. The major schemes for youth
development are: National Service Scheme, Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan, National
Integration Programmes, National Discipline Scheme, Youth Hostels and National Service
Volunteers Scheme, etc.

2.1 Many new initiatives have aiso been taken with a view to provide a new thrust to
the youth programmes. The Department has decided to set up Youth Development Centres
for a group of 10 villages each in order to give a fillip to participation of rural youth in
developmental activities. These centres will have facilities for information, sports, training
and youth programmes for rural youth. The land for the centre will be donated by the
Panchayats. This scheme will be implemented through Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan, an
autonomous Body under this Department.

2.2 The Department has also decided to add a few more important areas of national
priorities in the Action Plan of Nehru Yuva Kendras from the year 1994-95. These areas are:
Panchayati Raj Awareness, Health & Population Awareness, Vriksh Mitra Scheme for
environment promotion, SEWAK (Self Employed Workers Association Kendra), Youth
Festivals at block, district and national level, etc. Besides this, emphasis is being given this
year on making youth economically self-reliant.

Games & Sports

3. Sports is a State subject and as such development of sports is primarily the
responsibility of State Governments. The Department of Youth Affairs and Sports, however,
undertakes a number of programmes which aim at promoting sports activities, in the
country. It finances a number of such programmes including creation of sports infrastructure
various parts of the country, grants for laying of synthetic surfaces, spotting and nurturing of
excellence through various schemes of the Sports Authority of India (SAI), grants to
National Sports Federations for coaching camps, national championships, international
exposure and equipment purchase, grant of incentives in the shape of scholarships, cash
awards to eminent sportspersons, encouraging sports in the Universities by grants for
creation of infrastructure and holding of inter-University championships, organising
tournaments for rural youth, women and in the north eastern region. The Department has
launched a new scheme “Sports Fund for Pension to Meritorious Sportspersons” under

“ which Olympic Medalists and Gold Medalists of Asian Games are eligible for Life Pension
from the age of 30. The scheme is being operated through the Life Insurance Corporation of
India.

Youth Affairs
National Service Scheme (NSS)

4. The Committee is deeply concerned about the misutilisation and persistent failure of
the Department to appropriate resources allocated for the scheme during the last four years

1


and is constrained to observe that this is not a healthy phenomenon and should not be
allowed to continue any more.

4.1 The Secretary, Department of Youth Affairs & Sports, stated that the funds given
to the States were not being passed on to the Universities and also most of the Universities,
instead of giving money to Colleges, were utilising the money for purposes for which it was
not intended. It was further stated that the Department did not even get the required
feedback from the States about the money released to them.

4.2 The Committee is thus given to understand that, notwithstanding its earlier
recommendation to secure better cooperation from the States in operating this scheme, the
situation appears to have gone from bad to worse. The Committee is fully aware of the
practical problems involved in the entire process, yet it feels that the Department has failed
té make adequate efforts in this regard. Blaming the States and the Universities does not
solve the problem. It is also deplorable that the Department did not get any feed-back from
the States. The Committee is not satisfied with the performance of the Department in this
regard and recommends that it should make all-out efforts to prevail upon the States to
ensure not only proper utilisation of the grants but also to pass on sufficient feedback about
the progress of the scheme every year.

4.3 The Committee finds that the State Liaison Cells, which are basically meant for
maintaining coordination with various agencies involved in the scheme, in matters of timely
release of grants and proper implementation of the programme, were not doing their job at
all. The Committee emphasises the need to activate them.

4.4 The Committee is of the opinion that there is a need to recognise the NSS as a third
dimension of the academic activities and to provide incentives to NSS functionaries in
Universities and Colleges. The Committee feels that the recommendation of the expert
Committee, set up by the UGC on integration of NSS activities in Universities’ curriculum,
should be pursued effectively and vigorously.

4.5 The Committee also feels that the amount of Rs. 120 and Rs. 200, being provided
per volunteer per year for regular activities and special camps, needs to be substantially
increased to make the scheme attractive and their work specified.

Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan(NYKS)

5. Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan is one of the largest youth welfare schemes, run by
the Department which alone accounts for over one third of the total allocation for youth
welfare schemes. Several programmes of vital importance for non-student rural youth are
undertaken under this scheme.

5.1 The Committee finds, from the comparative statement on annual targets and
achievements during the last three years, that the targets of most of the programmes could
not be achieved during the years 1992-93, 1993-94 and 1994-95. The main reasons for the
shortfall ascribed by the Department were the uneven flow of funds to the NYKS and
vacancies of Youth Coordinators, particularly in the North Eastern States.

5.2 The Committee, after considering the matter, arrives at the conclusion that there
seems to be some slackness on the part of the Department and that it did not act as
responsibly as it ought to have been in this regard. The Committee desires that immediate
action should be taken to ensure an even and smooth flow of funds to the Kendras and
proper utilisation thereof.

5.3 In response to the Committee’s recommendation made last year for providing
adequate representation to the peoples’ representatives in the functioning of NYKs, the


Department informed the Committee that all the youth coordinators have been instructed to
involve peoples representatives in the programme. The Committee feels that simply
instructing the youth coordinators in such an important aspect, would not serve any purpose.
The Committee recommends that a proposal should be prepared with a view to associating
peoples’ representatives at different levels in the working of the NYKs. The Committee
reiterates its recommendation to make the functioning of NYKs more democratic and
transparent by introducing element of accountability in it.

5.4 The Committee feels that, in view of some new programmes (as mentioned in para
2.1) introduced under this scheme, the decrease in the allocation, both plan and non-plan,
this year would adversely affect the progress of the on-going as well as new programmes.
Therefore, the Committee recommends enhancement of the allocation for the scheme
adequately.

5.5 The Committee also recommends that the network of Programmes of Training in
Self Employment Project, Vocational Training and Youth Awareness drives should be
considerably expanded and strengthened so as to cover more and more youth of the country,
particularly in the rural and semi-urban areas, with the association of Panchayats and
Nagarpalikas.

5.6 The Committee is also of the view that the aims of the programmes of yocational
training and Training in Self-employment Projects overlap each other. Similar is the case
with schemes like Sports (Block level & District level) & Equipment Purchase and
Vocational Training and Sports Equipment Purchase. The Committee, therefore, suggests
that vocational Training and Training in Self-employment Project be merged, as well as
schemes like Sports (Block and District level) & Equipment Purhase and Sports Equipment
Purchase, with a view to avoiding duplication of activities in this regard.

5.7 The Committee is not aware if the Department is also assisting the youth trained
under the schemes of Vocational training and Training in Self-employment Project in setting
up income generating projects. If no such action is undertaken by the Department, the
Committee suggests that suitable action may be initiated to help them in this regard.

National Integration Programme

6. The Committee asked the Department to explain the reasons for reducing the
allocation for this programme, which aims at promoting national integration, from Rs. 525
lakhs in 1994-95 to Rs. 326 lakhs in 1995-96. The Department informed that the allocation
for this programme has been reduced this year because the provision for the NGOs has been
reduced from Rs. 265. Lakhs to Rs. 250 lakhs and that for the State Governments from Rs.
360 lakhs to Rs. 76 lakhs. This had to be done in view of the past experience where some
amount had to be surrendered due to lack of enough viable proposals from the States. Even
for a new component of Sadbhavana Shivirs, introduced in this programme, very few States
came up with viable proposals. As a result, the EFC, while approving the new component,
granted it for only one year on an experimental basis.

6.1 The Committee notes that while the reason attributed for bringing down the
allocation for the States was lack of enough viable proposals from them, no reason,
however, had been assigned for reducing the allocation in the case of NGOs. Whether it was
done due to resource crunch or their unsatisfactory performance is not clear.

6.2 The Committee feels that suitable programmes of interest to the youth be devised
with a view to promoting community living and sharing of common experiences.


Exhibitions for Youth

“7. When the Committee sought to know the reason for reducing the outlay for this
scheme from Rs. 30 lakhs last year to Rs. 15 lakhs in 1995-96, the Department gave the
usual reply that the allocation had to be reduced because not enough “viable proposals”
were received by the Department. It was further explained that many of the exhibitions,
related to the theme of National Integration, were held as a part of National Integration
Camps which were funded from the National Integration Scheme. In the Annual Action
Plan 1995-96 of the Department, the target had been brought down to 25 exhibitions only.
The Committee is not impressed by the reasons of viability given by the Department.
Besides, the term ‘viability’ does not appear to be appropriate.

7.1 The Committee is not convinced about the necessity for running such a programme
separately when the National Integration Scheme is taking care of funds for organising such
exhibitions. The Department does not appear to be very serious about continuing this
scheme, as it has brought down the target to just 25 exhibitions this year.

7.2 The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should examine the
matter with a view to merging this scheme with that of National Integration Scheme so as to
avoid unnecessary duplication which creates confusion and wastage of resources.

Scouting & Guiding

8. The Committee expresses its deep concern over the utilisation of only Rs. 60 lakhs
out of an amount of Rs. 92 lakhs allocated last year under this scheme. No plausible reason
was given for it except that the main beneficiaries of the scheme viz. Bharat Scouts &
Guides and All India Boys Scouts failed to utilize the full amount and expand their activities
despite all encouragement from the Department. The Committee feels that the scheme is not
functioning well and, therefore, recommends that the Department itself should make efforts
to pinpoint the factors responsible for the under-utilization and take corrective measures.
Evaluation of this scheme, undertaken by the Indian Institute of Management, be completed
early and followup action taken thereon.

‘Youth Clubs

9, The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the poor progress of this scheme, the
glaring example of which lies in the fact that out of the target of assisting 2,160 ‘Youth
Clubs, only 17 could be assisted till 7th December, 1994, as per the Performance Budget
1995-96 of the Department. However, in reply to a question, this figure was stated to be
950. The Committee fails to understand as to how the Department was able 10 cover 933
He ore clubs within a short span of three months. The Committee is constrained to observe
at the Dapartment is not serious about the progress of the scheme and recommends that it
should try to achieve the target set for this year and the allocated amount be utilised
properly.

9.1 The Committee was informed that the Youth Clubs in many States were facing
difficulties in getting themselves registered, being denied thereby any assistance under this
scheme. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should take up the
matter with the State Governments and help the Youth Clubs in getting the required
registration.

Training of Youth

10. This scheme is no exception to the general malady of under utilization of available
resources and failure in achieving the targets. The Committee observes that a large number
of youth in the country are sitting idle craving for proper training in self-employment
schemes whereas the Department absolves itself of all responsibility by saying that the target


could not be met since enough “viable proposals” were not received from NGOs and State
Governments. Release of only half of the amount (Rs.51.46 lakhs out of Rs.100 lakhs) and the
coverage of only one fifth Youth (1190 out of 5000 Youth) last year cannot be justified by any
means.

10.1 The Committee takes a serious view of the laxity and disinterestedness shown by the
Department in running this programme, in particular, and youth welfare schemes, in general,
and recommends that this state of affairs should not be allowed to persist uny more.

Youth Hostels

11. The main aim of this scheme is to promote youth travel with a view to promote national
integration. The Committee finds it to be a very good scheme and apreciates the decision on
retaining this scheme in the Central Sector. Financially, the scheme seems to have been affected
adversely in the process of its proposed transfer to the State Sector. The Committee was
informed that the Department had demanded Rs.100. lakhs more in addition to Rs.152 lakhs
provided in the BE last year, which it did not get. Only Rs.211. lakhs has been given this year.

11.1 The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should make all-out
efforts to make up this shortfall at the RE level, keeping in view the fact that 28 Youth Hostels
are under construction.

11.2 Keeping the objective of this scheme in view, the Committee had recommended last
year to locate these hostels mostly in places of cultural and historical importance. The
Committee reiterates that new hostels should be provided at places from where youths get a
glimpse of our religious and cultural diversities and glory of the past, and also get inspiration for
adventurist activities and also where infrastructure is not available at the moment. The
Committee feels that there is not much awereness about the existence of such hostels.and
procedure for getting the reservation etc. As a result, youths are not benefitting by the scheme
to the desired extent. The Committee therefore, recommends that the Government should take
necessary steps to publicise this scheme widely, utilising the mass media.

National Youth Awards and Awards to Outstanding Youth Clubs

12, The Committee finds the basic objectives of the two schemes laudable. The Department
had to slash down the allocation from Rs. 12.00 lakhs to Rs. 8.00 lakhs for the former and from
Rs. 40.00 lakhs to Rs. 30.00 lakhs for the latter this year. The Department stated that it was
done in keeping with the progress 0 expenditure last year.

12.1 The Committee feels that the progress of these schemes has not been satisfactory. It
appears that either the Department was not able to identify sufficient number of deserving
youths and youth clubs for giving awards or they were not able to fulfil the standard laid down
by the Department to qualify for these awards.

12.2 The Committee is of the opinion that motivation, which these awards aim at, is the
sine-qua-non of good performance. It, therefore, recommends that the Department should see
to it that selection of sufficient number of youths and Youth Clubs was down and awards given
to them every year.

Assistance to Voluntary Organisations Working in the Field of Youth

13. In response to a query regarding department not being able to achieve the target for
covering the stipulated number of youth in 1994-95 under this scheme, the Committee was
informed that this scheme was entirely NGO dependent and that the target for 1994-95 of
covering 20,000 youths had to be brought down based on the past experience in thls regard and
also due to more emphasis now on long-term training programmes with lesset number of
beneficiaries.


13.1 The Committee was informed that this scheme is very popular among the NGO
as a result of which allocation for this scheme was enhanced from Rs. 55 lakhs in 1994-6
to Rs. 72 lakhs in 1995-96. The Committee notes that the Department has increas
allocation for this scheme without any major increase in its total allocation and also th
funds were fully utilised in the previous year. The Committee is satisfied with the progre
of the scheme. It however, recommends that the Department should try to strengthen the
scheme and ensure that the funds were not misutilised possibilities of which connot b
ruled out.

National Discipline Scheme

14. The Committee is surprised to find that Rs. 9.66 crores have again been provided
for this scheme in the year 1995-96. The Department pleaded that it had to be done
because it was committed to meet the expenditure on pay and allowances etc., of the
Instructors so long as they remained in services. The Committee fails to understand the
need for spending more than nine crores every year for a scheme which is non-existent and —
the Instructors of which have been absorbed in the respective State services. Last year also
the Committee had recommended to take this scheme out of the Department’s purview.
The Committee , therefore, reiterates that the Department should take up this matter wil
bai Ministry of Finance and the States with a view to shifting this scheme to the Stat

‘or.

Games And Sports

15. The Committee notes that the total outlay (Rs. 132.74 crores), provided in th
Department’s BE for the year 1995-96, is less than that (Rs. 135.11 crores) in the outgoing
financial year. हि

15.1 The Committee was informed that it was firstly on account of the Finan
Ministry’s refusal to provide an amount of Rs. 3.00 crores which was projected as dues to
the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, and secondly, the Ministry of Finance was of the vi
that the Department should generate its own resources for the purpose. There is now son
kind of a mandate with the Planning Commission that while the total outlay, under th
Rlan, of smaller Departments (like the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports) should be
fixed at a certain level, increase should be allowed only for major Departments. The
general feeling is that any organisation which is capable of generating its own reven
does its job better.

15.2. The Sports Authority of India, under the Department of Sports, ‘is today
generating a certain level of revenue by adopting what is called “pay and play” policy in
differant stadia. Stadia are also rented out for benefit matches and for cultural activities.
Another method is renting out buildings not required on day-to-day basis. For example,
the Delhi Stock Exchange and the Al). India Council of Technical Education are
functioning from SAI buildings. Nehru Yuvak Kendra is also housed in one of SAI
building’. Receipt from all these sources during 1993-94 and 1994-95 was Rs, 2.05 cro:
and Rs. 6.00 crores respectively, The Department expects to earn Rs. 8 crores in 1995-!

15.3. The Department runs a number of important and useful schemes which aim
inter- alia at developing in the youth qualities of discipline, self-reliance, justice and fair
play, besides imparting appropriate professional and vocational training with a view to.
enabling them to avail of.a suitablé employment. The Committee feels that irivestment in
youth development, in fact, is a very vital and long term investment. The Committee doe:
not know the basis on which the Planning Commission had decided that the Department ०|



Youth Affairs and Sports is a small Department and hence no increase is necessary in its
outlay. The Planning Commission appears to have failed to appreciate the need for
increasing the allocation for the Department. Such inadequate outlay would certainly affect
sports activities adversely when there is so much criticism of India’s performance in
international events.

15.4. The Committee feels that there is greater need to lay more emphasis on sports
activities for which the funds provided for the year 1995-96 are inadequate. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Department should take up the matter at the appropriate
level and try to convince the Ministry of Finance to increase the allocation suitably at the
R.E. level, so that atleast the important and major schemes/programmes of Department do
not suffer due to.lack of funds.

15.5. The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department for raising its revenue
by renting out its stadia and buildings. It, nevertheless, feels that such practice should not
affect the sports activities adversely. The Department may frame certain rules and
regulations in this regard which should be observed strictly. A Marketing Cell may also be
created in the SAI which will be responsible for not only the commercial exploitation of
stadia but also of exploring other avenues for raising more revenue.

Sports Project Development Area (SPDA)

16. This scheme aims at providing basic facilities at its various centres for a
comprehensive and integrated system of coaching and training to talented young sports
persons in the age-group of 9-14 years. The Committee notes that out of 78 centres
sanctioned, only 34 centres had been set up so far. The Committee had pointed out this fact
in its Sixth Report on the Demands for Grants of the year 1994-95 also.

16.1. The Department informed the Committee that the successs of this scheme
depended Jargely upon the participation of the States and that its working had been
evaluated by the Tata Consultancy Services. The Department is now considering to replace
SPD centres with 78 Sports sub-centres by dovetailing this scheme with Sports Hostel and
Special Area Games (SAG) Schemes.

16.2. The Committee agrees with the proposal of amalgamating the above three
schemes as it would not only provide all the facilities at one place to children and youth for
developing their talent, it would also avoid duplication of work and facilities. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that, in view of the importance of the scheme, the
proposal should be approved and implemented at the earliest.

16.3. The Committee also suggests that atleast one such centre should be set up in
every State, in the first instance, and rest of them may be set up in stages depending upon
the requirement of the States.

Rural Sports Programme

17. Out of Rs. 100 lakhs provided for this scheme in 1994-95, only Rs. 10.3 lakhs could
be utilized by 31st December, 1994. Rs. 100 lakhs has been provided again for this scheme
in 1995-96. When the Committee enquired about the reason for this gross underutilisation of
funds and the justification for demanding Rs. 100 lakhs again, it was explained that the
underutilization under this scheme was due to unspent balance from the previous years
available with the SAI under Rural Sports Tournaments and also due to paucity of “viable
proposals” for assistance to rural sports clubs. The Department hoped, however, that the
position would improve this year, as more States were expected to take the bénefit under
the component of Rural Clubs and there would not be any unspent balance available with
SAI for organising the tournaments in 1995-96


17.1 The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the money remaining unspent at
ultimately surrendered, particularly when the Department wants more money, whereas
remain unutilized q

17.2 The Committee is not satisfied with the reasons given by the Department for
underutilisation of funds and feels that it was either due to inadequate publicity of the
scheme in the rural.areas or because of delays caused due to stiff conditions imposed in
processing the proposals

17.3 The Committee fails to understand the basis for the optimism expresséd by th
Department that there would be enough proposals next year and that it would be able to
utilise the entire amount provided for this purpose in the year 1995-96,

17.4 In view of this, the Committee strongly recommends launching of a massive
publicity campaign about this scheme in rural areas through suitable means and feels that
involving Panchayats in this regard should also be considered हे

17.5 The Committee is of the opinion that indigenous sports do not mean a kho-kho
and kabaddi. Every State has different kinds of local games, gymnastic skills and martial arts”
which have survived through the ages among the village people who have a very high degree
of excellence in them. The Committee is distressed to find that these indigenous rural sports
which do not require a great deal of investment, are not being encouraged by th
Department adequately. Sufficient money should be earmarked for creating sports
infrastructure in rural areas.

17.6 The Committee further notes that the Department does not have any scheme ६
providing sports facilities in the urban slum areas. Youth and children, due to lack of spa
in slums, do not have any physical activities at all. The Department informed the Committ
that there was no proposal at the moment for this.

17.7 The Committee recommends that the Department should take immediate steps i
this regard as the lack of sports activities in slums gives rise to many undesirable
consequences and problems. There is an urgent need to channelise the energy of youth livin
in urban slums for constructive purposes.

Accountability

18. In its Sixth Report on Demand for Grants for 1994-95, the Committee had
mentioned about the lack of accountability and coordination among. the various sports
bodies. The Department in its reply, has stated that in a scenario where the performance
depended upon the joint effort of the National Sports Federations, Sports Authority of India
Coaches, Department of Youth Affairs and Sports, it has became difficult to bring about —
accountability for poor performance: ॥

18.1 The Secretary agreed with the Committee that somebody had to be made
accountable for the poor performance. Unfortunately, the way the system is working, it is
not really possible to do that. It is the National Federations, however, that are responsible
for bringing up the teams to a certain level. The Sports Authority of India, in fact, is mainly _
responsible for bringing out talents at the young age, and provide them the basic facilities
and inputs. Boys and girls having good potential are given exposure and training at th
centres of excellence. Thereafter, it is really for the Federations to select teams (one
nominee is there in the selection committee) and hold the caoching camps. The SAI gives a
necessary assistance and facilities for holding the national or international championsh
also. But when there is a failure, nobody could really be found accountable, as
there are many interconnecting factors. 7


18.2 The Committee inferms from the above that the Department also admits that there
is no accountability in the system. The Committee feels that any system without the element
of accountability is bound to prove disastrous and this is what is happening in the
Department. The Committee does not agree with the contention of the Department that due
to many agencies/bodies involved in promotion of sports it is not possible to identify and fix
responsibility on any one of them.

18.3 The Committee deplores the manner in which the entire system is being run where
not only there is no accountability but there is no coordination among the various agencies
responsible for promotion and development of sports in the country. There appears to be a
slinging match between various sports federations and the SAI. One generally blames the
other for encroaching upon each other’s spheres.

18.4 The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the possibilities of having a
coordinating body at the national level be explored and suggests that an expert committee be
set up to look into the reports submitted by the coaches/managers and sports administrators
after each international tournament with a view to fix responsibility for poor performance
and to pin-point reasons therefor so that effective remedial measures could be taken.

18.5 The Committee is separately examining the issue of India’s poor performance in
international sports. Eminent sportsmen and administrators are being invited by the
Committee to give their views in this regard. The Committee proposes to deal, in that
report, with various aspects of sports organisation and management in the country, including
the role of SAI and sports federations, Ministers and Secretaries heading sports bodies,
talent search, training, infrastructure, excessive exposure to certain games to the detriment
of others, incentives to sportsmen to adopt sports as a career, introduction of sports as a
compulsory subject in school and college curricula, role of private sector in sports
promotion, etc. Hence the Committee is not spelling out is views on these aspects in the,
present report. :

Exchange of Sports and Physical Education Team

19. This scheme has been described by the Department to be a ‘big leap forward’ in
providing the much needed opportunities for foreign exposure to our teams and obtaining
services of competent coaches/experts. It is also said to have been proved to be very
beneficial to our sportspersons.

19.1 The Committee asked as to how can the reduction in allocation for stich a useful
scheme from Rs. 173 lakhs (BE) to Rs. 125 lakhs at the RE level in 1994-95 be justified. It
also wondered as to why had only Rs. 55 lakhs been spent till November, 1994 and asked if
the Department would be able to spend the rest of the money in the remaining four months
of the financial year 1994-95.

19.2 The Department explained that the outlay was reduced in the RE keeping in view
the.progress of expenditure in the previous year. It was not clear to the Committee as to
why the expenditure in this regard was slow and what had the Department done with a view
to speeding it up.

19.3 The Committee recommends that the Department should make all out efforts to
see to it that the funds are fully utilised and the good schemes like this should have targets
fixed every year. a
Promotion of Sports and Physica! Education Among Women & National Sports Championship
for Women

20. The Committee notes that while National Sports Championship for Women is given


Rs. 56 lakhs per year, only Rs. 3 lakhs are given to the scheme for Promotion of :
and Physical Education among Women.

20.1 The Committee wished to know as to why have the financial outlays for th
schemes for the year 1995-96 remained the same as they were in the outgoing fin
year. The outlays for these schemes according to the Department, were based on a
pattern of assistance and as such there were no changes in the outlays. The sche
envisaged providing scholarships etc. and the conduct of championship at district, state
and national level for each of which a fixed amount is released.

20.2 The Committee fails to appreciate the logic behind adopting fixed pattern of
assistance to these schemes. The Committee is of the opinion that with the present level
of allocation, the Department would not be able to attract more and more women to the
field of sports. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the fixed pattern of
assistance should not be applied to these schemes which are meant specifically for
women.

20.3 The Committee gathers the impression, from the reply submitted by the
Department, that both of these schemes were being pursued in a half-hearted. and
mechanical manner. The need of the hour, the Committee feels, is to inculcate a sense
of confidence and leadership qualities among women for empowering them in an effective
manner. Promoting sports and physical activities among them is the best way to achieve
this. The Committee feels that these schemes need to be strengthened, both by providing
more funds and also by extending them to the lower level. 7

NCC Junior Division Troops

21. The NCC organisation aims at imparting training to the youth in public
residential central schools and colleges so as to make them disciplined citizens. |

21.1 The Committee was informed that the maintenance of these troops was funde¢
by the Ministry of Defence and Department of Youth Affairs & Sports. As regards
criteria for selecting the schools, the Department stated that they were placing the cual
at the disposal of DG, NCC and the Ministry of Defence was fixing the criteria. |

21.2 The Committee was given to understand that the Department was not aware 0
the criteria for selecting schools for this purpose. If it was so, the Committee expresse
its unhappiness as the Department bears 60% of expenditure on this scheme. It is als
not known to the Committee whether the Ministry of Defence was consulting ०
associating DYA & S while fixing the criteria for selecting schools/colleges. Th
Committee, therefor, feels that there is a need to have greater interaction an
coordination between both the Ministeries in this regard.

National Federations

22. The Committee pointed out that there had been a shortfall in utilising Rs. 90
lakhs under plan and Rs. 85 lakhs under non-plan, provided in the year 1994-95, fo
giving grants to various National Federations and asked the Department the reasons fo
the reduction in the outlay for this purpose in the year 1995-96.

22.1 The Committee was informed that Rs. 900 lakhs provided for this 7
under plan would be fully utilised by the end of year 1994-95. However, under non-pl
there was likelihood of Rs. 30 lakhs remaining unspent on account of receipt
insufficient proposals from the Federations. ५

22.2 The reduced outlay for this scheme in 1995-96 is due to the refusal of |
Planning Commission to increase the total outlay of the Department. It is also’



possible to reduce the allocation under the heads like SAI, STCS and Incentives for
Promotion of Sports activities and so there is no scope for diversion either.

22.3 The Committee is fully aware of the overall resource crunch in the Government of
India and that the Department had to allocate the amount to different schemes/programmes
whatever it had got from the Planning Commission. The Committee, however, is baffled to
learn that an amount of Rs. 30 lakhs remained unspent last year on the plan side because
sufficient proposals were not received from the Federations, particularly when they complain
that they were not getting adequate fund for their activities. Whatever might have been the
reasons for this, the Committee considers it as a serious lapse on the part of both the SAI
and the Federations. The Committee is of the opinion that both of them should have seen
that the fund was fully utilised.

General Observations/Recommendations

23. When asked if the Department had any proposal for involving elected Nagar Palikas
and Panchayats in implementing various schemes/programmes, the Committee was apprised
that at present, under the Scheme of Grants for Creation of Sports Infrastructure, proposals
of local bodies and voluntary organisations were being considered. Besides, under the
scheme of Rural Sports Programme, rural clubs at the Panchayat level were also being
assisted. However, the Department pleaded that it would not be possible to release funds
directly to the Panchayats, as it would be difficult to monitor the utilisation of funds by these
bodies from the Central Government.

23.1 The Committee feels that these local level elected bodies could be very effective
and useful in getting the various schemes of the Department implemented, particularly in
tural and semi-urban areas.

23.2 The Committee, therefore, suggests that the Department should examine this
aspect and come out with a comprehensive proposal outlining the manner in which the
services of these bodies could be utilised by the Department, of course, under proper
supervision and control.

24. The Committee notes with great concern that there has been underutilisation of
funds provided to the Youth Affairs and Games and Sports. It also notes that the reason
cited for this has invariably been the non-receipt of so called viable proposals / response
from the States. Such a state of affairs, the Committee realises, is causing considerable
damage to the implementation of the schemes and_lot of funds are being either not utilised
or misused. The Committee is of the view that the responsibility for this falls squarely on the
Department and it cannot get away simply by saying that States are not cooperating. The
Committee therefore, recommends, that the Department should act more responsibly and
the States should be more responsive in this regard.

25. The Committee has observed that in view of a plethora of schemes / programmes,
both under Youth Affairs and Sports, sometimes the activities of some of them overlap with
one another, which leads to unnecessary complication and confusion adversely affecting the
implementation thereof. This also results in wastage of scarce resources. In view of this, the
Committee suggests that the Department should undertake a general review of all the
schemes in whose case there is a duplication of activities and merge them to the extent
possible:

 CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH  HAVE  BEEN ACCEPTED BY GOVERNEMNT
 
VIII.    BALIKA SAMRIDDHI YOJANA (BSY)
 
RECOMMENDATIONS /OBSERVATIONS
 
8.6         The Committee is of the opinion that the final decision about its status should be taken without any further
delay.  It should not happen that the Tenth Plan period is also over and no decision has been  taken.  Level of allocation
in 2005-06 (Rs. 3 lakhs) hints at this possibility only.  The Committee would also like to mention that continuance of
unspent balances cannot be considered an ideal position.  Such a position confirms the inability of implementing
agencies to administer the scheme. The Committee also feels that in the event of a decision being taken for continuance
of this Scheme, then very effective monitoring mechanism and also sufficient publicity for making the targeted
beneficiaries aware will have to be an essential component of the Scheme.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
              The suggestions of the Committee are noted for compliance, if the Scheme is continued and implemented, at

XIII.    CENTRAL SOCIAL WELFARE BOARD (CSWB)
 
RECOMMENDATIONS /OBSERVATIONS
 
13.3       The Committee feels that the working of the Central Social Welfare Board and its state counterparts needs to be
further strengthened and their network may be utilized for monitoring implementation of different schemes of the
Department at different levels.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The suggestion of the Committee has been noted.
 
XVI.    NATIONAL NUTRITION MISSION
OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
16.5     The Committee notes the implementation of the scheme at snail pace.  It seems no specific purpose is being
performed by the mission since some of the objectives are already covered under the scheme of ICDS.  The Department
should strive to define its target/ objective and then implement the scheme.
ACTION TAKEN
            The National Nutrition Mission (NNM) was constituted under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Prime Minister in
July, 2003.  Recently, a Cell called “Food and Nutrition Security Watch” has been set up in the Planning Commission to
keep a watch on implementation of major programmes relating to food and nutrition security.
            In the light of this development a view has to be taken whether the issue of food and nutrition security has to be
handled through the NNM or through the Cell being set up in the Planning Commission.  This matter is under active
consideration of Government.
            However, the concern of the Committee has been noted.
CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH  THE COMMITEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN
VIEW OF GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
 
III.       INTEGRATED CHILD DEVELOPMENT SERVICES (ICDS)
 
RECOMMENDATIONS /OBSERVATIONS
 
3.7.        Another disturbing feature is acute shortage of Anganwadi workers.  Out of 23,265 sanctioned posts of
supervisor, as many as 10,965 are vacant, with maximum number of vacancies being in Bihar and UP.  The Committee
notes that EFC note on this issue has been forwarded to the Planning Commission and other Ministries for their
comments.  Comments of the Planning Commission are awaited.  EFC note will be sent to CCEA for final approval. 
The committee is of the view that there should be more focus on operationalising of ICDS projects and AWCs.  Efforts
should be made atall levels-Central, State and district level to operationalise all sanctioned and proposed additional
projects/AWCs.
 
ACTION TAKEN
The ICDS functionaries are State Govt. employees and the  responsibility for filling up the vacant posts  lies
with the State Governments.

I            BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
           
1.1       The Committee notes that Plan allocation of Rs. 6000.00 crore made in BE 2004-05 for the Department of
Elementary Education and Literacy was increased to Rs. 8000.00 crore at the RE stage.    It has been further enhanced to Rs.
12531.76 crore in BE 2005-06.    The Committee is happy to learn that about 98 percent of this fund had been utilized till 30
March, 2005 under 'Elementary Education'. Under the head 'Adult Education' the performance of the Department is not
equally impressive as only 77.95% of allocated funds were utilized till 18.3.05. The Committee is, however, surprised to
note that utilisation under Adult Education jumped to 92 per cent in a span of just 13 days, i.e., between 18 and 30 March,
2005.
ACTION TAKEN
            It is correct that the utilization of funds in Adult Education picked up in the later half of November, 2005 and more
than 94.59% of the grant was utilized by 31.3.2005.  The reasons for increase in expenditure during this period are as
follows:-
(i)  The last meeting of  Project Approval Committee of NLMA was held on 31.1.2005. Hence, the grant to such districts
whose proposals were approved by the PAC on 31.1.2005 could only be released in March.
 
(ii) Proposals for release of grant are processed only after settlement of accounts in respect of earlier grant.  In cases where
Audited Accounts furnished by districts were not complete, clarifications were sought from the districts.  Release of further
grants was processed after the requisite information was received from the districts. 
 
(iii)  Special efforts of the districts and State Literacy Mission Authorities/State Governments in the month of March for
submission of required documents/ information to NLM also resulted in higher release of grants in the month of March.

VI.       DISTRICT PRIMARY EDUCATION PROGRAMME  (DPEP

6.2       The Committee was informed that the reviews and various evaluatory studies of the programme have shown
significant increase in enrolment, improvement in learning achievement, reduction in repetition rates/drop-outs with
increased community involvement, improvements in classroom processes, etc.  The Committee does not agree with these at
all because the facts in certain respects do not support these conclusions.  Despite the increase in enrolments over the years,
the average Student Class Ratio (SCR) for schools covered under DPEP has come down from nearly 50 in 1996-97 to 42 in
2002-2003.  Also, the dropout rate of children between grade I toV, has been found to be between 10-20 per cent in one third
of the districts covered under the programme.  The Committee desires that the Department should look into the factors for
dropouts and remedy the situation by making schools attractive to the child.  The Committee is not ready to buy the off-
repeated argument that poverty and illiteracy of the parents are the main factors for dissuading child from studies.  In fact,
The Committee is of the considered view that the poor and uneducated today, in fact, are more eager to send their children to
schools.
          
ACTION TAKEN

VII      MAHILA SAMAKHYA
 
RECOMMENDATIONS /OBSERVATIONS
 
7.5       To a question regarding the targets fixed for the Xth Plan period and the achievements thereof in respect of Mahila
Samakhya, the Department had stated the following:
"No targets are fixed under the Mahila Samakhya scheme as the MS scheme adopts an innovative approach, which
emphasizes the process rather than mere fulfillment of targets.  Education in Mahila Samakhya is not merely
acquiring basic literacy skills but is a process of learning to question, critically analyzing issues and problems and
seeking solutions.  It allows the women to learn at their own pace, set their own priorities and seek knowledge and
information to make informed choices."
ACTION TAKEN
 
                                                In the Mahila Samakhya programme, no targets are set by the Government of India or State Governments in a conscious
resolve, to allow grassroot women to set their own priorities and plan their targets for action.  The local level aspirations, are
reflected through a process which culminates in the State Mahila Samakhya Programmes’ annual work plan.  This work
plan, its physical & financial aspects are reviewed  & monitored by Government of India & the State Mahila Samakhya
Programme regularly. 
            There are, therefore, certain “enabling processes” and a set of “annual programmative interventions” that are
monitored annually.
RECOMMENDATIONS /OBSERVATIONS
 
7.6       The Committee is not inclined to agree with the contentions of the Department given above, which appears to be an
attempt to mystify the whole thing.  After all, basic aim of the programme is to enable our women, most of whom are in
rural areas, illiterate, poor, with little powers either in their family or in the society.  The Committee fails to comprehend as
to how the Department proposes to enable such target groups to learn to question critically, analyzing issues and
programmes and seeking solutions, set their own priorities, seek knowledge and information, to make informed choices, etc. 
The Committee feels that there has to be some kind of enabling activities for achieving these objectives. The Committee is
of the firm opinion that it is possible to fix targets in respect of those activities both in terms of number as well as time-
schedule. The Committee is surprised to see that it has not been done.  The Committee reiterates, as it has done in this report
in the case of DPEP, that such kind of open -ended approach without fixing targets would lead us nowhere.  It, therefore,
recommends that targets and time-schedule may be fixed for this scheme also.   
 
ACTION TAKEN
The core activities of the programme centre around issues of health, education of women and girls, accessing public
services, addressing issues of violence and social practices which discriminate against women and girls, gaining entry into
local governance, seeking sustainable livelihoods etc. The enabling activities of the programmeare:
·
           Formation of Women’s collectives (Sanghas) by women facilitators (Sahyoginis) for mobilizing women.
·            Dissemination of information, awareness building and facilitating collective action on core themes indicated above.
·            Development of supportive structures such as     Mahila Shikshan Kendras for the education of older girls and young
women who have never been enrolled or have dropped out of school, setting up Nari Adalats for addressing issues of
violence against women, etc.
MS scheme has been designed to evolve targets for its annual programmatic interventions through decentralized
planning. Women in the Sanghas at the village level identify the key areas around which thematic inputs are required, and
these inform the development of the Annual Work Plan and Budget of each State MS Society. The AWP and Budget of each
State reflects targets in:
a)      The number of new villages where programme activities are to be initiated and the number of new ‘sanghas’ that are
to be formed.
b)      The number of trainings to be conducted for Sangha/Federation women in the core thematic areas,
c)      The number of facilitative structures like Mahila Shikshan Kendras, Nari Adalats etc. to be established,
Due to decentralized nature of planning for programmatic interventions, there is no prescription of targets based on
uniform parameters for all MS States. However, each State MS Society does have  targets for each of its District

In the Tenth Plan, two targets regarding geographical expansion and baseline surveys have been set.  With regard to
