V.        RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL CRECHE SCHEME FOR THE CHILDREN OF WORKING MOTHERS
 
5.1       Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme for the Children of Working Mothers was launched with effect from 1
st January 2006 after merging the National Creche Fund and the Scheme of Assistance to Voluntary Organizations for Creche for Working and Ailing Women’s Children. The new scheme provides improved services and enhanced financial allotments besides increasing the number of crèches in the country. The financial norms have been revised from Rs. 18,480/- to Rs. 42,384/- per crèche per annum. It has been decided to set up 14,719 new crèches by the end of Tenth Plan. Eligibility criteria for those entitled to
availing services under the new Scheme have also been enhanced from Rs. 1800/- to Rs. 12,000/- per month.
5.2       The allocation for BE 2006-2007 has been enhanced to Rs. 81.00 crore for setting up of proposed crèches by the end of Tenth Plan across the country and for meeting expenditure required on enhanced norms.  Against an allocation of Rs. 31.50 crore in 2005-2006 Rs. 28.50 crore were utilized. The Committee would, however, like to point out that uptil 31
st December, 2005, utilization figures stood  at Rs. 10.03 crores.   However, thereafter, in the last quarter of the year, Rs. 18.47 crore were released.   The Committee is not happy with this uneven spread of fund allocation.   Besides, the Committee  is also constrained  to observe
that allocation meant for NE states has remained underutilized during the last few years, with nil expenditure been reported during 2004-05 and 2005-06. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for non-utilisation of funds in NE region.
5.3       The Committee notes that the Ministry kept an ambitious target of 14719 creches by the end of Tenth Plan i.e. by 2006-2007; the new crèches will be allocated to the Central Social Welfare Board, Indian Council for Child Welfare and Bharatiya Adim Jati Sevak Sangh in the ratio of 80:11:9. The Committee would like to be apprised about the rationale of selecting only three agencies for operationalising the Crèche Schcme. The Committee further recommends that more and more reputed and established NGOs may be selected for implementing the Creche Scheme.
5.4       To strengthen monitoring of crèches, the scheme provides engaging of independent monitoring agencies. These agencies will be identified in consultation with the concerned State Governments and will conduct regular monitoring of crèches. In the course of inspection, these agencies are expected to assess the motivation and capacity of the implementing agencies also. It is expected that every crèche will be inspected at least once in a period of two years.
5.6       The Committee is satisfied with the steps taken to strengthen the monitoring of scheme, but has its reservations about the actual implementation aspect. It is surprising that the scheme has started functioning but consultations with State Governments are yet to take place. The Committee recommends that a time schedule may be prepared urgently in consultation with State Governments and implementing agencies for implementing its various aspects of the scheme. The aspect of utilization of funds also needs to be addressed properly.
5.7       The Committee understands that out of 4885 creches sanctioned under NCF (National Creche Fund), 2514 creches having completed five years were not receiving any grant from the NCF as they had submitted an undertaking that they would run the crèches on self-supporting basis after five years. The Ministry clarified that crèches sanctioned under National Crèche Fund have been merged with the revised crèche scheme namely Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme for the children of working mothers, with effect from 1.1.2006.
5.8       The Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensure that  2514 creches which were earlier provided grants are not given further grants under the New Scheme. The monitoring process need to be strengthened and responsibility fixed for any delay.
5.9       With a view to provide better services, to build up child friendly environment in the Creche Centre and to orient the crèche workers as well as the implementing agency, the component of a short term training has been added to the new Scheme. The training module will be prepared with the help of National Institute of Public Cooperation and Child Development and the training will be organized through the agencies identified in consultation with the concerned State Government.
5.10     The Committee recommends that the training module should be finalised in a time frame and a suitable plan of action devised so that the targets of the training are achieved.
           
VI.       CONDENSED COURSES FOR WOMEN EDUCATION
 
6.1       The Scheme of Condensed Courses for Women Education was initiated by CSWB in 1958 to cater to the needs of adult girls/women who could not join mainstream education system or who were dropouts from formal schools. The scheme aims to provide educational opportunities to girls/women above the age of 15 years alongwith additional inputs of skill-development/vocational training. The main focus of the scheme is to ensure that contents of the courses are need-based and modified according to local requirement and simultaneously targeting towards various stages of education levels of primary/middle/high school and
matric/secondary level courses.
6.2       Plan allocation of Rs. 5.40 crore was made for this programme in 2005-2006. The actual expenditure incurred upto 3
rd March 2006 is Rs. 2.70 crore. The Ministry has informed that sanctions were being issued and entire allocation was to be utilized by 31.3.2006.The Committee has, however, some reservations on the last minute spending by the Department. Rushing the expenditure in the last few days needs to be discouraged for effective utilization of resources.
6.3       The Ministry informed that in pursuance of the recommendations of National/State level workshops, a National Working Group has been constituted for revamping/evaluation of the scheme in the changing socio-economic and work environment. The report of the Working Group which was expected in August 2005 is yet to be submitted. The Committee is unhappy over the delay in submission of the Report and recommends that the matter be expedited without further delay. The Committee would also like to be apprised of its contents as and when the report is finalized.
6.4       The Committee has been given to understand that no residential course has been sanctioned to any State Board by CSWB in recent years due to paucity of funds as it involves more than double of the amount meant for Non-residential courses and the allocation under the programme is very limited and hardly sufficient to meet the demand of all the States.
6.5       The Committee is not happy with the present state of affairs. It feels that residential courses on selected basis should be sanctioned in those States where the response is encouraging. Obviously the girls/women are unable to pursue their studies further because of lack of hostels. The residential courses can help them fill the gap. The Committee further recommends that additional funds may be sought for the purpose.

VII.     BALIKA SAMRIDDHI YOJANA
7.1       The scheme was launched in 1997 with the aim of raising the status of girl children in Below Poverty Line families. The scheme was reviewed and recast in 1999.  Subsequently, as a  consequence of decision taken by the Planning Commission to relocate some of the Centrally Sponsored Schemes to the States, BSY was selected to be one such scheme and it was proposed to be transferred w.e.f. 2005-06
7.2       In 2004-05, funds were released to States, however no funds were kept in BE 2005-2006 and 2006-2007. The Ministry has informed that no monitoring/publicity was undertaken at central level.  The Committee observes that total funds released as on 1.3.06 is Rs. 216.15 crore whereas unspent balance as on 30.9.2005 is Rs. 74.97 crore lying with different States like Bihar, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Orissa and Uttaranchal.
7.3       Earlier the Committee in its 160
th Report had expressed serious concern about the implementation as well as the aspect of uncertainty in the transfer of BSY to the States. The Committee observes that situation instead of improving has worsened since no decision has been taken in this regard so far. The Secretary in her appearance before the Committee also conceded that this was a very unsatisfactory status.
7.4       The Committee is not happy with the uncertainty status of the BSY scheme, continuing for so long.  The Committee fails to understand as  why Planning Commission has taken such a long time to take a decision on transferring the Balika Samriddhi Yojana to states.  A decision taken by the Planning Commission at the beginning  of the Tenth Plan is yet to be finalized even though Tenth Plan period is in its  last year. The Committee is also not aware as to how the Committed Liability of Rs. 74.97 crore    lying with different states is going to be adjusted.   The Committee is of the view that this is a classic case of improper
formulation of a scheme launched in haste and inherent flaws being noticed during the course of its implementation.   The Committee does not have much hope about this scheme being effectively implemented by states, with  some States already facing severe financial constraints.   The Committee would once again reiterate that fate of BSY scheme needs to be decided at the earliest.   The Ministry being the nodal authority has to vigorously pursue this issue with the Planning Commission.

9.2       The allocation in 2005-2006 was Rs. 15.00 crore whereas the expenditure incurred upto 3.3.2006 was Rs. 12.38 crore. The allocation for 2006-2007 has been kept as Rs. 16.00 crore. The Ministry has cited the following reasons for low utilization.

The requests for release of 2
nd and subsequent installments are not received with UCs of earlier grants sanctioned, audited statement of accounts, physical and financial progress reports duly countersigned by the State Government/Department, monitoring Committee reports, concurrent evaluation report, etc.

XI.       CENTRAL SOCIAL WELFARE BOARD (CSWB)
11.1     The CSWB was established as an interface between the Government and the voluntary sector to promote social development in the country. The Board is involved in the implementation of a number of programmes such as  Border Area Projects, Family Counselling Centres,  Working Women Hostels, Swawlamban and Swahadhar etc. CSWB implements the various programmes of the Ministry. These programmes are implemented through voluntary organizations in collaboration with State Social Welfare Advisory Boards. The Committee was informed that the Ministry has not made any effort to strengthen the network of
CSWB and its State counterparts for monitoring implementation of different schemes of the Ministry at different levels.
11.2     The allocation for the year 2005-2006 was Rs. 34.43 crore against which expenditure reported upto 31st December, 2005 is only Rs. 15.79 crore.  For the year 2006-2007 the allocation was reduced to Rs. 23.45 crore. The Ministry has informed that due to closure of Border Area Projects and Demonstration Projects w.e.f. 1.4.2005, provision has been reduced.
11.3     As per information available to the Committee, unspent Balance of Rs. 34.96 crore under various programmes are lying with the CSWB which includes Rs. 11.76 crore under the Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme and Rs. 12.81 crore under  Short Stay Homes.
11.4     The Committee observes that CSWB is entrusted with the implementation of large number of schemes. The assignments have been spread to such an extent that CSWB has failed to devise proper monitoring mechanism for such schemes. CSWB is a central organisation directly under Ministry’s control and it is very surprising to the Committee that the Ministry has not made any effort to strengthen the network of CSWB.   It would be a better situation, according to the Committee, if CSWB is asked to focus its attention on onespecific assignment for a particular period of time. Declining Girl child ratio is a problem which is
assuming alarming proportion nation- wide. The Committee notes some initiative have been taken by a few States for improving the lot of girl child. But some sort of scheme totally dedicated for development of girl child needs to be initiated at national level. The Committee feels that CSWB can play a major role by focusing on this social problem. Nationwide campaign by CSWB in co-ordination with all States Boards and other concerned agencies will have a lasting impact on the thinking of public at large. The issue of huge unspent balances with the different agencies of CSWB would be addressed in case its mandate is specifically
defined. The Committee would, therefore, appreciate if the Ministry identifies some focused subjects for implementation by CSWB.

rd March 2006 is ‘NIL’. RELIEF AND REHABILITATION OF VICTIMS OF RAPE
15.4     The Committee also notes that a scheme for the relief and rehabilitation of victims of rape is proposed to be introduced in compliance with a judgment of the Supreme Court delivered in the year 1994 which directed the Government to bring forward such a scheme specially considering that some of the victims of rape are too traumatized to continue in employment. The special feature of the scheme is an award of monetary compensation to the victim apart from rehabilitative action.
15.5     The Committee feels that the victims of rape undergo the conditions of psychological stress and trauma notwithstanding the physical assault. XVI.    PREVENTION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT AT WORKPLACE
 
16.1     The Government of India constituted a Central Committee under the Chairpersonship of the Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development to monitor the implementation of the Supreme Court’s Guidelines for prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace. The Committee in its Meeting held on 29.10.2002 recommended that Awareness needs to be given on this issue and this task had been assigned to National Commission for Women (NCW) and Central Social Welfare Board alongwith Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The National Commission for Women has taken up sexual harassment of
women at work place as one of the focal issues in the realm of promotion of gender equality and women's empowerment.  The Commission had widely circulated the Visakha Judgement for compliance along with a code of conduct for workplace formulated by the NCW. The Committee is not aware of the activities/initiatives undertaken by the CSWB and Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to create awareness on the SC Guidelines. This has become all the more important in view of increasing incidents of sexual harassment in BPOs and other private institutions.
16.2     The Committee has been informed that in order to assess the extent to which guidelines and norms laid by the Apex Court have been implemented as well as to share the experiences/ difficulties faced by various organizations in dealing with complaints of sexual harassment, the Commission has been holding meetings with various Organisations/Government Departments since November, 2000. XVIII.GENDER BUDGETING
18.1     Women face gender specific barriers to access of public services and expenditure. Gender Budgeting lends itself to strengthening of administrative processes and actions achieve the targets for improvement in the position of women. It not only entails a look at allocation of resources for women but goes beyond to cover tracking the utilization of allocated resources, impact analysis and beneficiary incidence analysis of public expenditure and policy from a gender perspective.
18.2     Gender budget has been conceived as one of the tools for achieving the goals and targets set in our plans and policies benefiting women. The basic intent is to achieve the objectives enshrined in the Constitution towards overall development of women. The Committee appreciates that the Ministry has undertaken a number of measures for achieving the targets of gender budgeting.
18.3     The Committee notes that during 2005-06, as a result of persistent efforts made by the Ministry Gender Budget Cells have been set up in 41 mainstream Departments  including Power, Petroleum, Culture, Heavy Industries, Science and Technology etc.
18.4     The Committee recommends that being the nodal Ministry, the Ministry of WCD should ensure that Gender Budget Cells which are set up in the Ministries have become operational and also pursue this issue with the remaining Ministries.
18.5     Committee’s attention has been drawn by a few gender concerns that the Ministry has raised with various Ministries in Government of India as indicated below:
-           Secretary, Sports and Youth Affairs has been addressed on the need for raising participation of women in sports and according due recognition to success stories.
 
-           The subject of Health Insurance Scheme for women in view of their vulnerabilities and barriers to access to medical services has been raised with Secretary (Health).
 
-           The Planning Commission has been requested to engender State Plans.
 
-           Secretary (Exp.) and Member-Secretary Planning Commission have both been requested to include a column on gender outcomes in the Outcome Budget of GOI
 
The Committee would like to be apprised about the implementation status of the aforesaid initiatives taken by the Ministry.
18.6     Committee’s attention has been drawn by the details regarding scheme-wise provisions and physical targets benefiting women in the Budget of Ministry of Women and Child Development as given in the Performance Budget (2006-07). The Committee finds that all the schemes whether targeting children or women have been shown to be providing 100% benefit to women alone. The Committee does not dispute the fact that welfare ofthe child is ultimately the welfare of its mother.However, in view of the emerging concept of child budgeting, it cannot be claimed that flagship schemes like ICDS are benefiting cent percent
women.The Committee recommends that the allocation on programmes and schemes benefiting women may be delineated specifically. The Committee also recommends that the components of gender budgeting may be made more clear and included in the guidelines for gender budgeting.

III.                   INTEGRATED CHILD DEVELOPMENT SERVICES (ICDS) SCHEME
 
                        The Committee was informed that the Inter-Ministerial Task Force set up in 2004 to review the existing population norms for sanction of an ICDS Project/AWC and suggest revised norms had submitted its reports/recommendations in May 2005. The Committee finds that so far 23 States/UTs have undertaken a micro-level Survey/Planning and forwarded information regarding location specific requirement of additional ICDS Projects and Anganwadi Centres. The Committee has been given to understand that information submitted by some States is incomplete and not in the prescribed format. One year has passed since
the submission of the Report of the Task Force, and the required information is still awaited from States/UTs. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry should make concerted efforts so that AWCs can be set up as per the revised population norms.                                               (Para 3.5)
 
                        The Committee notes that from 2005-2006, the Government of India were to support States upto 50% of the financial norms or 50% of the expenditure incurred by them on supplementary nutrition. The Committee is surprised to note that the Ministry has not held pre-budget discussions with the States on this issue so far. Ministry’s clarification that States can present their resource position during their discussion on the States Annual Plan with the Planning Commission is not at all convincing.                  (Para 3.6)
 
                        In the absence of any detail about the supplementary nutrition met by the States/UTs, it is difficult to assess the impact of the new initiative. The Committee would like to be apprised of the implementation status of this initiative during 2005-06.                                                                                                                      (Para 3.7)
            The Committee agrees that increasing the number of Anganwadi Centres from existing 7.44 lakhs to 14 lakhs may be a gigantic task but the Ministry can no longer afford to sit on the problem and delay the process. Instead a plan of action needs to be formulated by the Ministryexpeditiously for achieving the targets set by the Supreme Court. Implementation of the SC directives would catapulate the health of the Indian population comparable to the standards of any of the developed countries. The Committee therefore feels that the Ministry should study the suggestion in its entirety and chalk out a road map to implement the
same. Lack of funds can not be the sole excuse to implement the suggestion. The Committee would also like to be apprised of the reply given to the Supreme Court by the Ministry in this regard. The Committee desires that Anganwadi Centres may be immediately made operational in hemlets and tribal areas where concentration of Dalits, SC/ST population is high.                    (Para 3.9)
 
            Keeping in view the special needs in NE States, the Central Government sanctioned construction of 4800 AWCs at the cost of Rs. 60 crore in 2001-2002 and 7600 AWCs at a cost of Rs. 95 crore in 2002-2003. Another 7600 AWCs at a cost of Rs. 95 crore have been sanctioned in 2004-2005. Further it has been decided to undertake construction of AWCs @ Rs. 1.75 lakh per center. Funds would be allocated out of savings available in the NE component of plan budget of the Ministry. The Committee hopes that in NE States all the AWCs would be provided with  pucca buildings. (Para 3.10)
                        The Committee is equally shocked to see the findings of the NCAER. The Committee would like to point out that these findings are not restricted to the infrastructure status of AWCs. It is very clear that each aspect about the AWCs has been assessed and reported upon. This Report has been received by the Ministry sometime in March-April 2005. The Committee hopes that findings of this survey must have been shared with the State Governments and follow-up action started. If not, it may be done at the earliest. The Committee would like to be apprised in this regard at the
earliest.                                                                                                           (Para 3.13)
                        The Committee is of the considered opinion that the large number of responsibilities entrusted with the Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) will seriously affect the primary work of the Anganwadi Centres(AWCs) for which they were mainly appointed. With the burden of large number of additional duties the AWW can do justice neither to AWCs nor to the additional responsibilities. The Committee notes that the Central Government provides an honorarium of Rs. 1000 p.m and Rs. 500 p.m to an AWW and AWH respectively. This is quite meager an amount compared to the burden of responsibilities entrusted on them. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the honorarium paid to these two important functionaries of AWCs may be suitably increased. A hike in their remuneration would help in increasing their motivation for better results. Resource constraints should not come in the way of such justified increase.                      (Para 3.15)
           
                        The Committee expresses its deep anguish over the large number of vacancies of AWWs, AWHs and Supervisors. It would not be wrong to conclude that the vacancies have hampered the functioning of AWCs and adversely affected the scheme itself. The Committee is not aware about the factors responsible for such a state of affairs. In the absence of these key functionaries, an AWC can not be considered to be operational. The Committee wonders in what manner and by when it would be possible to fill up this big gap, specially in view of 1,88,055 AWCs sanctioned in 2005-06, with the figure likely to increase further. 
The Committee is of the firm view that the exercise of sanctioning and filling up of these posts should start simultaneously with the sanctioning of AWCs. Otherwise this shortfall will always persist. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that an intense drive needs to be launched for filling up the vacancies within a fixed time frame. This can be accomplished if a strategy is worked out in collaboration with the State Governments/local bodies. Those States which are not willing to follow the time schedule may be pursued on regular basis, if need be, at the highest level, till the vacancies are filled up. The Committee would like
to be apprised of the steps proposed to be taken.       (Para 3.18)
 
                        The Committee is happy to note the decision of convergence between ICDS scheme and SSA & DPEP. The success of ICDS programme depends purely on effective supervision, monitoring, co-ordination and convergence with other Departments and also with better and effective participation of local bodies and community. Convergence of various components is a good idea. The Committee recommends that the revised guidelines, if need be, may be issued without any delay and the State Governments and implementing agencies be pursued for smooth implementation of the converged scheme. Keeping in view the
expansion of the ICDS scheme and its proposed convergence with other programmes, the Committee strongly feels that an effective monitoring mechanism at all levels need to be put in place at the earliest. Only then, services envisaged under ICDS scheme can reach the intended beneficiaries. The Committee would like to be apprised about the steps taken in this direction.                                                                                                                (Para 3.20)
 
                        The Committee would like the Ministry to take cognizance of the observations contained in the Mid Term Appraisal and take immediate remedial measures to streamline the scheme. The Committee desires that it may be apprised about the steps taken in this direction.                                                                (Para 3.22)
 
                        The Committee observes that in 17 States/UTs, Co-ordination Committees at state, district, block and village levels have been set up to ensure convergence between ICDS, Health, Drinking Water and Sanitation, Panchayati Raj, Primary Education, Rural Development etc. Welcoming the initiative taken by these 17 States, the Committee would like to point out that NE States, Sikkim, J&K, Orissa and Southern States have not come forward so far. The Committee hopes that with the matter being pursued by the Ministry, these States will be covered very soon.           (Para 3.23)
 
                        The Committee understands that a study on ‘Three Decades of ICDS: An Appraisal’ has been conducted in all the States/UTs. Draft Report was likely to be completed by the end of March 2006. The Committee would like to be apprised about the findings of this study as and when finalised and reported.                                          (Para 3.24)

st December, 2005, utilization figures stood  at Rs. 10.03 crores.   However, thereafter, in the last quarter of the year, Rs. 18.47 crore were released.   The Committee is not happy with this uneven spread of fund allocation.   Besides, the Committee  is also constrained  to

                        In 2004-05, funds were released to States, however no funds were kept in BE 2005-2006 and 2006-2007. The Ministry has informed that no monitoring/publicity was undertaken at central level.  The Committee observes that total funds released as on 1.3.06 is Rs. 216.15 crore whereas unspent balance as on 30.9.2005 is Rs. 74.97 crore lying with different States like Bihar, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Orissa and Uttaranchal.                         Earlier the Committee in its 160
th Report had expressed serious concern about the implementation as well as the aspect of uncertainty in the transfer of BSY to the States. The Committee observes that situation instead of improving has worsened since no decision has been taken in this regard so far.                         The Committee is not happy with the uncertainty status of the BSY scheme, continuing for so long. VIII.    ASSISTANCE FOR CONSTRUCTION/EXPANSION OF HOSTEL BUILDINGS FOR WORKING WOMEN WITH DAY CARE CENTRES FOR CHILDREN
 
The Committee finds that both the financial and physical performance under the scheme have shown declining trend over the years. The utilization has been below the target.   It seems that there is no activity under this scheme in the NE region  as there was an expenditure of only Rs.9 lakhs against an allocation of Rs.1.00 crore in 2004-05 and nil expenditure  has been reported in 2005-06 as on 3.3.2006. The Committee is not aware whether any exercise has been initiated so far to make an assessment about the unsatisfactory performance of this scheme  and take remedial measures.   If not, done so far, the Committee feels that this is
the right time to initiate the same.     (Para 8.1)
 
                        The Committee was informed that there are 40 projects sanctioned from 2001-2002 to 2005-06 in the implementation stage under the Scheme of Working Women Hostel. Out of these projects, in respect of 17 projects, either the file is not traceable or no progress report has been received so far. In majority of these cases, implementing agencies are NGOs.  There are a few  cases where expenditure has already exceeded  the original estimate  and the building project is not yet complete.    The Committee has been informed that in most of the cases, organizations involve their own construction agency for the construction of
hostel building. Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) in its Report No. 2 of 2004 (Para 6.5) has also criticized  the Ministry for its failure to monitor the utilization of grants totalling Rs. 39.58 crores given to NGOs and local bodies for construction of hostels for working women.  The Committee is surprised to note that the requisite information is still awaited from most of the States.                                    (Para 8.2)
 
                        The Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry should not finance such projects or scheme, wherein it has no control over its implementation. In the present scheme, the Committee feels the accountability is lacking and control is missing. Implementation Agencies should not have the sole discretion to select construction agencies.   In any case, projects need to be handled by Government agencies. The Committee would also like to point out that there is an increasing need for setting up more Hostels. If need be, norms for opening of Hostels can be reviewed and revised. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the scheme needs to revamped and started afresh.                                       (Para 8.4)

XVI.                PREVENTION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT AT WORKPLACE
 
                        The Government of India constituted a Central Committee under the Chairpersonship of the Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development to monitor the implementation of the Supreme Court’s Guidelines for prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace. The Committee in its Meeting held on 29.10.2002 recommended that Awareness needs to be given on this issue and this task had been assigned to National Commission for Women (NCW) and Central Social Welfare Board alongwith Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The National Commission for Women has taken up sexual harassment
of women at work place as one of the focal issues in the realm of promotion of gender equality and women's empowerment.  The Commission had widely circulated the Visakha Judgement for compliance along with a code of conduct for workplace formulated by the NCW. The Committee is not aware of the activities/initiatives undertaken by the CSWB and Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to create awareness on the SC Guidelines. This has become all the more important in view of increasing incidents of sexual harassment in BPOs and other private institutions.(Para 16.1)
                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                        The Committee is constrained to observe that that the Supreme Court Guidelines had not been properly followed both by the Government Departments.  In a number of cases, Complaint Committees had not been formed.  Where these committees existed, they did not have 50 per cent reservation for women.  Also in many cases the Committees were headed by men instead of women and without the involvement of a third party (NGO).  Lack of awareness among the Members of the complaint Committee was also noticed. The Committee is of the firm view that Supreme Court directive needs to be implemented in letter
and spirit.   The Committee would like to have full details about the 799 organisations covered so far by the NCW alongwith theorganizations where complaint Committees are yet to be set up.    The Committee would also like to have an idea about the additional organizations covered by NCW. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should come forward with a comprehensive legislation for prevention of sexual harassment in work places. The private institutions may also be brought under the purview of the legislations related to prevention of sexual harassment.   (Para 16.5)

                        Committee’s attention has been drawn by the details regarding scheme-wise provisions and physical targets benefiting women in the Budget of Ministry of Women and Child Development as given in the Performance Budget (2006-07). The Committee does not dispute the fact that welfare ofthe child is ultimately the welfare of its mother.However, in view of the emerging concept of child budgeting, it cannot be claimed that flagship schemes like ICDS are benefiting cent

REPORT
I           INTRODUCTION
1.1       The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports was set up as the Department of Sports in 1982 at the time of
organisation of the IX Asian Games in New Delhi.   Thereafter, during the celebration of the International Youth Year
in 1985, it was converted into the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports. It became a full-fledged Ministry on the 27 th
May, 2000.
1.2       The Youth i.e. those falling within the age group of 15-35 years constitutes nearly 40% of the total population of

176th Report of Committee on Human Resource Development
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/176threport%20.htm[01-07-2016 15:28:47]
the country.   To optimally tap the constructive and creative energies of this most valuable human resource, the Ministry
of Youth affairs and Sports has taken a number of new initiatives since its inception.    The Ministry organises a large
number of programmes in the field of youth development, sports and physical education.
1.3       The Joint Secretary (Sports), while deposing before the Committee, highlighted the various activities undertaken
by the Ministry during the year 2005-2006. He informed the Committee that Nehru Yuva Kendra played a major role in
providing relief materials, organizations of camps, counselling and career guidance to Tsunami victims.  SAI hostel,
Port Blair acted as both the center for housing inmates and for giving relief to Tsunami victims.  Contribution made by
NYK in providing relief to the earthquake victims in Kashmir was also worth-mentioning. Another initiative taken by
the Ministry was identification of Sports Federations performing well for giving them additional Funds.
1.4       A mention was also made about the new initiatives planned for 2006-07. A new Scheme ‘Yuva Shakti Abhiyan’
was going to be launched in Panchayats in all the States. Similarly all the Youth organizations like NYKS, NSS, NCC,
Bharat Scouts and Guides are being involved in the campaign on HIV/AIDS. States are going to be involved more and
more in the monitoring of different schemes.  He also drew the attention of the Committee towards the commendable
performance of Indian players who won a total of 50 medals and retained 4
th position in Commonwealth Games held at
Melbourne, 2006. These achievements were made possible to a large extent by the financial assistance made available to
the Sports Federations by the Ministry and also providing the necessary facilities to the participating players.
II.         BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
2.1       The total outlay, both Plan and Non-Plan taken together provided to the Ministry for the year 2005-2006 was Rs.
506.99 crores which was reduced to Rs. 478.01 crores at RE stage.  The expenditure booked upto 20
th March 2006 was
approximately Rs. 413 crores which means the Ministry was supposed to spend  Rs. 93 crores in remaining 11 days of
last financial year. The allocation for 2006-2007 is Rs. 669.00 crores (Plan Rs. 600.00 crores and Non Plan Rs. 69.00
crores). The Ministry informed thatagainst a projected demand of Rs. 929.29 crores under Plan for the year 2006-2007 a
provision of only Rs 600.00 crores has been made.   The projections were made, taking into consideration, higher
requirements for a number of ongoing and proposed schemes to be implemented by the Ministry during 2006-2007.
2.2       The Ministry informed that the cut made in the actual allocation from the proposed allocation would definitely
hamper proper implementation and ultimately have a negative impact on performance of the following schemes:
(Rs. in crores)
 Proposed Actual Allocation
SAI 173 150
Creation of Sports infrastructure 90 27
Commonwealth Games 200 150
Training of Indian Athletes 75                      --
            Not only this, proposed expansion of NYKS to 123 uncovered districts and promotion of Rural Sports Club
movement in the Villages would also be adversely affected due to the cut in the proposed demand of the Ministry.
Activities proposed to be initiated under the Action Plan for Youth to combat HIV/AIDS epidemic in the country were
also going to be restricted. The Committee notes that no allocation has been made for Training of Indian Athletes
against its proposed allocation for Rs. 75 crores. Such sweeping cut may have some concrete reason. The Committee
presumes that the Ministry have some contingency plans to arrange the finance for the Training of Indian Athletes for
the forthcoming Asian, Commonwealth Games and other International events. The Committee would like to be apprised
of such plans/scheme.
2.3       The Committee is aware that under the Constitution, Sports being a State subject, State
Governments/autonomous organisations/NGOs have to play a very active role in the implementation of the different
Youth and Sports related schemes.  The Committee observes that Tenth Plan Outlay of Rs. 1825.00 crore is more than
double of the Ninth Plan allocation of Rs. 826.09 crore for the Ministry.   Whereas there has been optimum utilisation of
allocated funds during the Ninth Plan, position is somewhat different during the Tenth Plan.  Plan allocation of Rs. 600
crore for 2006-07, last year of the Tenth Plan, is at a very enhanced level when compared with the previous  years of the
Tenth Plan.  The Committee notes that the allocations remained underutilised inspite of reduced projections at the RE
stage as indicated below –

The Committee fails to understand the constraints being faced by the Department in the optimum utilisation of
allocated funds for Youth and Sports related schemes. It remains a guess work for the Committee whether the under-
utilisation is due to the inability of implementing agencies (both Govt. & private sector) to take the full benefit of these
schemes or inherent flaws in the scheme itself are attributed to the same. The Committee observes that funds remained
underutilised under the schemes of Promotion of Adventure Activities, Promotion of Scouting and Guiding, National
Service Volunteer Scheme, Promotion of Youth Activities and Training, Rashtriya Sadhbhavna Yojana, Assistance to
Rural Youth and Sports Clubs, Scheme for welfare and development of Adolescents, Grants to Sports Federations. What
is more worrisome is that under Schemes like National Sports Championship for Women, National Welfare Fund for
Sportspersons, Promotion of Sports among Disabled, Scheme relating to Talent Search and Training, Scheme for Dope
Test, All India Council for Physical Education, and States Sports Academy expenditure remained nil. The Committee
also finds that provision made both under Youth and Sports Scheme for NE States remained underutilized.
 2.4      The  Committee can  afford to conclude that even the formulation  of   a  quarterly  annual   action  plan for 2005
- 2006 by the  Ministry  has  not  been  able  to  achieve  the desired results. It’s the case of failure in planning.  It
appears to the Committee that the Ministry remained engaged in projecting higher requirements and launching   new  
schemes without any considerations of the judicious and  optimum  utilisation  of  funds  allocated  for the existing
schemes. It is quite contradictory that on one hand the Ministry talk of resource crunch and on other hand the allocated
resources are not fully utilized.  Huge unspent balances are lying with the Ministry under various schemes.  This fiscal
disorder in the Ministry has done more harm. The case for higher allocations has weakened to a great extent.  The
Committee is of the view that a detailed review of all the ongoing schemes should be undertaken so as to assess the
shortcomings being noticed and take remedial steps for removal of the same.   Active involvement of the State
Governments and other implementing agencies in this exercise is called for. The Committee would like the Ministry to
adopt better fiscal management practices to avoid the last minute spending for achieving the targets.
III        NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR YOUTH
3.1       Report of the National Commission for Youth was laid on the Table of both the Houses of Parliament on
23.12.2004.  Fourteen recommendations made by the Commission have been accepted by the Ministry in principle
which include:-
-
                     Setting up of Rashtriya Yuva Kosh on the pattern of the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh;
-                      Expansion of National Service Schemes in all universities and colleges and scheme to be introduced at
class IX level and amalgamation of NSS & NCC Comments of the Ministry of Defence to be asked for
and to make serving either NSS or NCC mandatory for every student to become eligible for award of
degree.            
3.2       The Committee finds the recommendations made by the Commission very useful in empowering the youth. 
Unfortunately not much progress has been made in the implementation of these recommendations.  No follow-up action
appears to have been taken after the meeting with the officials of the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh on the feasibility of
formulation of Rashtriya Yuva Kosh.  Similarly the proposal with regard to amalgamation of NSS and NCC sent to the
Planning Commission simply remained a referral. The Committee would like the Ministry to expedite the action on all
recommendations particularly with regard to setting up of Rashtriya Yuva Kosh. The Committee feels that either the
NCC or NSS should be made compulsory from class IXth.
IV.       NEHRU YUVA KENDRA SANGATHAN
4.1       Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS),  an autonomous body of the Ministry which functions in Districts all
over India is engaged in conducting various youth programmes. Being the largest grass root level organization in the
world it is presently catering to the needs of more than 8 million non-student rural youth enrolled through about 2.30
lakh village based youth clubs.  The vast network of the youth clubs is the real strength of NYKS.
4.2       NYKS accomplishes its task through three categories of programmes i.e. Regular Programmes such as, Youth
Club Development, Vocational Training, Work Camp, Awareness Generation, Cultural Programme, Sports Promotion,
Adventure Promotion, Seminars and Workshops and Celebration of National and International Days/Weeks; second
category of schemes include National Service Volunteers, Financial Assistance to Youth Clubs, Awards to Outstanding
Youth Clubs at District, State and National levels, Rural Information Technology and Youth Development Centres
assigned to it by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports for implementation.  The third category being the special
programmes undertaken in collaboration with other Ministries and Organizations.
4.3       An allocation of Rs. 34.00 crores was made at BE and RE stage during 2005-06. The actual expenditure was Rs.
33.21 crores.  The allocation for 2006-07 is Rs. 45 crores against proposed outlay of Rs. 61.18 crores.  The Committee

4.5       The Committee notes that the achievement level both physical and financial under most of the programmes
undertaken by NYKS does not present a healthy picture.  In most of the cases the targets are fixed at very high level and
the achievement level is very low.  In some programmes the achievement level is even less than 10%.  The Committee
takes a serious note of it and recommends that in future more realistic target level should be fixed.  The Committee is
constrained to note that the percentage of women beneficiaries in some of the States under certain programmes is even
nil.  The overall coverage of women amongst 8 million rural youth covered presently under NYKS is also poor.  The
Committee reiterates  its earlier recommendation to enhance the level of female beneficiaries under various
programmes run by NYKS. 
4.6       Committee notes that two computer programmes viz
 Vocational Training Centres (VTC) and Rural Information
Technology Youth Development Centres (RITYDC) are being run by NYKS for imparting computer literacy to the
rural youth. 7855 youths have been benefited through 125 Vocational Training Centres run by District NYKs. Under the
second programme, 500 RITYDCs are proposed to be set up by the end of 10 th five-year plan out of which 164
RITYDCs have been established.  Through these centres, the youths of adjoining villages are getting training on
computer use, internet facility and some basic software programmes like MS word, Excel and Power point. A grant of
Rs.1.20 lakh is provided to each RITYDC therefor.
 4.7      The Committee appreciates successful operation of these two schemes aiming at computer awareness amongst
the rural youth.   However, the coverage as well as the spread of centers is not quite encouraging.  Only 164 RITYDCs
could be put in place upto December,  2005 against a target of 500 centres during the entire plan period. The Committee
has all doubts that the remaining 336 RITYDC would be set up by the end of 10
th five-year plan.  There is no denying
the fact that the Ministry needs to fix such realistic targets, which are achievable. 
4.8       The Committee had occasion to study the following details of unspent balances under different schemes of
NYKS.

4.9       The Committee regrets that this unhealthy trend of unspent balances in NYKS goes against the Ministry’s

176th Report of Committee on Human Resource Development

mandate for youth development planning. Under-utilisation of funds not only undervalues the scheme but also de-
motivates the implementing agencies as well as the beneficiaries. It reflects poor level of coordination amongst the
implementing agencies and ineffective monitoring at the Ministry’s level.  The Ministry need to take constructive steps
to encourage the field level functionaries with a view to effectively plan the programmes round the year and
implement them as per the prescribed norms. 
4.10     The Committee notes that Nehru Yuvak Kendras are proposed to be set up in 123 uncovered Districts, 15 being
in Orissa, 16 in UP, 10 in Arunachal Pradesh, 8 in Chhattisgarh and 8 in MP. The Committee was informed that a
proposal involving annual expenditure of Rs. 492.67 lakhs and non-recurring one time expenditure of Rs. 123 lakhs for
creation of 123x3 posts for these Kendras has been submitted to Ministry of Finance.  The Committee would like to
remind the Ministry on the controversies arose during its last selection process of Youth Coordinators.  The confusion
and uncertainity over the last recruitment process is still not over. The Committee feels that the court cases pertaining to
last recruitment of Youth Coordinators need to be pursued vigorously for early settlement. The Ministry, needs to be
equally cautious about its fresh proposal of recruitment with the Finance Ministry so that the process of selection
remains transparent and does not raise any doubts. The Committee would appreciate if a status report on the issue is
submitted for its consideration.
4.11     The Committee has been emphasizing in its earlier Reports the need for strengthening the monitoring
mechanism of NYKS by association of elected representatives.  The Committee understands that instructions have been
issued to the District Youth Coordinators to involve M.Ps, MLAs and other public representatives in the activities of
NYKS.  District Youth Coordinators are also supposed to send the minutes of the meetings of the District Advisory
Committee for Youth Programmes to respective MPs/MLAs.    The Committee would like to have an idea about the
level of compliance of these instructions by the District Youth Coordinators.
V.        NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME
5.1       The Scheme is targeted towards students of Universities, Colleges, +2 level schools and institutions of higher
learning in all the States/Union Territories.  Volunteers are enrolled for undertaking Regular activities and Special
Camping Programme under the Scheme which included social work like blood donation, Adult and Non-formal
education etc.
            The main objectives of National Service Scheme (NSS) are:
(a)
            understand the community in which they work;
(b)           understand themselves in relation to their community;
(c)            identify the needs/problems of the community and involve them in problem solving;
(d)           develop among themselves a sense of social and civic responsibility;
(e)            utilize their knowledge in finding practical solutions to individual and community problems;
(f)             develop competence required for group living and sharing of responsibilities;
(g)            gain skills in mobilizing community participation;
(h)            acquire leadership qualities and democratic attitudes;
(i)              develop capacity to meet emergencies and natural disasters and
(j)             practise national integration and social harmony.
 
5.2       An allocation of Rs. 31.50 crores has been made for NSS under plan in 2006-2007 against a provision of Rs.
26.10 crores last year. The allocation this year has been kept on higher side due to the increase in the enrolment of
students in various universities and colleges.  Also there is a proposal to introduce National Service Scheme from IXth
class onwards. The Committee would like the Ministry to consider introduction of NSS from class IX itself in the
light of noble objectives of the scheme.
5.3       The Committee notes that the motto of NSS “Not Me But You” reflects the essence of democratic living and
upholds the need for self less service.  NSS helps the students develop appreciation of other person’s point of view and
also show consideration to other living beings.  The philosophy of the NSS is well doctrined in this motto, which
underlines the belief that the welfare of an individual is ultimately dependent on the welfare of the society on the whole
and, therefore, the NSS volunteers  strive for the well being of the society.
5.4       The Committee understands that there is a need to deploy more number of National Service Volunteers who act
as link between the Kendra and village based Rural Youth Clubs.  The Committee strongly feels that it is high time for
acknowledging the good work being done by NSS volunteers. Their efforts need to be encouraged and commensurated
with good incentives. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the incentive given to NSS volunteers should be
enhanced and brought at par with the incentives provided to the NCC cadets so that they perform their duties with
greater zest and vigour.

5.5       The Committee notes the following constraints being experienced by the Ministry in the implementation of NSS

VI.       NATIONAL DISCIPLINE SCHEME
6.1       The National Discipline Scheme was originally started in 1954 by the Ministry of Rehabilitation, which was
later transferred to Ministry of Education and Social Welfare in 1958. Consequent upon the recommendations of Dr.
Kunzru Committee in 1963, introducing discipline programme at school stage, the integrated scheme called “National
Fitness Corps” (NFC) was evolved.  The Scheme was transferred to the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports (Now
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports) in eighties when a separate Department was formed.
6.2       On the basis of the recommendations of Dr. Kunzru Committee, the decision to transfer NDS Instructors to
various State Governments was taken in consultation with the State Education Secretaries.  In the year 1969, the Central
Cabinet took a decision that the employees under the NFC would be transferred to the services of the State Governments
on the condition that the Central Government would reimburse their pay and allowances so long as they remained on the
strength of the State Governments. The Committee was informed that 6145 NDS Instructors were transferred to various
State Governments after decentralization of NDS scheme.
6.3       Though physically the NDS Instructors were absorbed in the services of the State Governments, the Central
Government was committed to bear the liability of their pay and allowances and this system has been continuing since
seventies. Due to inadequate budgetary provisions, the Central Government has never been able to bear its liability to
the fullest extent and thereby the accumulated liability continued to grow to unmanageable level. The Committee was
informed that the total liability towards pays and allowances for States of M.P., Punjab, Haryana, H.P., Rajasthan,
Kerala and Maharashtra from which information has been received is to the tune of Rs. 184.21 crores. Information from
remaining ten States is yet to be received. The total projected liability in respect of all the States is to the tune of Rs. 300
crore. A budget support would be required on that account.          
6.4       The Committee regrets that repeated reminders from the Department to some States have not evinced any
response and the issue of committed liabilities remains un-resolved for years together. The Committee feels that this
situation of uncertainty should come to a halt. A time has come when the Ministry should fix a final deadline for such
States to avoid this never-ending chaotic scenario. The Ministry should settle the issue once for all after paying the
liabilities to those States who have furnished the information. The States who do not respond may have to forgo their
claims. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would plan the whole process to ensure settlement of committed
liabilities within this financial year itself. The Committee would also like the Ministry to appeal to the States to avail
this opportunity and expedite their claims without further loss of time.

the under-utilisation is due to the inability of implementing agencies (both Govt. & private sector) to take the full
benefit of these schemes or inherent flaws in the scheme itself are attributed to the same. The Committee observes that
funds remained underutilised under the schemes of Promotion of Adventure Activities, Promotion of Scouting and
Guiding, National Service Volunteer Scheme, Promotion of Youth Activities and Training, Rashtriya Sadhbhavna
Yojana, Assistance to Rural Youth and Sports Clubs, Scheme for welfare and development of Adolescents, Grants to
Sports Federations. What is more worrisome is that under Schemes like National Sports Championship for Women,
National Welfare Fund for Sportspersons, Promotion of Sports among Disabled, Scheme relating to Talent Search and
Training, Scheme for Dope Test, All India Council for Physical Education, and States Sports Academy expenditure
remained nil. The Committee also finds that provision made both under Youth and Sports Scheme for NE States
remained underutilized.                                                                       (Para 2.3)
                        The  Committee can  afford to conclude that even the formulation  of   a  quarterly  annual   action  plan
for 2005 - 2006 by the  Ministry  has  not  been  able  to  achieve  the desired results. It’s the case of failure in planning. 
It appears to the Committee that the Ministry remained engaged in projecting higher requirements and launching   new  
schemes without any considerations of the judicious and  optimum  utilisation  of  funds  allocated  for the existing
schemes. It is quite contradictory that on one hand the Ministry talk of resource crunch and on other hand the allocated
resources are not fully utilized.  Huge unspent balances are lying with the Ministry under various schemes.  This fiscal
disorder in the Ministry has done more harm. The case for higher allocations has weakened to a great extent.  The
Committee is of the view that a detailed review of all the ongoing schemes should be undertaken so as to assess the
shortcomings being noticed and take remedial steps for removal of the same.   Active involvement of the State
Governments and other implementing agencies in this exercise is called for. The Committee would like the Ministry to
adopt better fiscal management practices to avoid the last minute spending for achieving the targets.(Para 2.4)
III        NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR YOUTH          
                        The Committee finds the recommendations made by the Commission very useful in empowering the
youth.  Unfortunately not much progress has been made in the implementation of these recommendations.  No follow-
up action appears to have been taken after the meeting with the officials of the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh on the feasibility
of formulation of Rashtriya Yuva Kosh.  Similarly the proposal with regard to amalgamation of NSS and NCC sent to
the Planning Commission simply remained a referral. The Committee would like the Ministry to expedite the action on
all recommendations particularly with regard to setting up of Rashtriya Yuva Kosh. The Committee feels that either the
NCC or NSS should be made compulsory from class IXth.
                                                                                                                             (Para 3.2)
IV.       NEHRU YUVA KENDRA SANGATHAN
                        The Committee notes that the achievement level both physical and financial under most of the
programmes undertaken by NYKS does not present a healthy picture.  In most of the cases the targets are fixed at very
high level and the achievement level is very low.  In some programmes the achievement level is even less than 10%. 
The Committee takes a serious note of it and recommends that in future more realistic target level should be fixed.  The
Committee is constrained to note that the percentage of women beneficiaries in some of the States under certain
programmes is even nil.  The overall coverage of women amongst 8 million rural youth covered presently under NYKS
is also poor.  The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation to enhance the level of female beneficiaries under
various programmes run by NYKS.                                                                                      (Para 4.5)
                        The Committee appreciates successful operation of these two schemes aiming at computer awareness
amongst the rural youth.   However, the coverage as well as the spread of centers is not quite encouraging.  Only 164
RITYDCs could be put in place upto December,  2005 against a target of 500 centres during the entire plan period. The

176th Report of Committee on Human Resource Development
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/176threport%20.htm[01-07-2016 15:28:47]
Committee has all doubts that the remaining 336 RITYDC would be set up by the end of 10 th five-year plan.  There is
no denying the fact that the Ministry needs to fix such realistic targets, which are achievable.
                                                      (Para 4.7)
                        The Committee regrets that this unhealthy trend of unspent balances in NYKS goes against the
Ministry’s mandate for youth development planning. Under-utilisation of funds not only undervalues the scheme but
also de-motivates the implementing agencies as well as the beneficiaries. It reflects poor level of coordination amongst
the implementing agencies and ineffective monitoring at the Ministry’s level.  The Ministry need to take constructive
steps to encourage the field level functionaries with a view to effectively plan the programmes round the year and
implement them as per the prescribed norms.                                                                                                 (Para 4.9)
                        The Committee notes that Nehru Yuvak Kendras are proposed to be set up in 123 uncovered Districts, 15
being in Orissa, 16 in UP, 10 in Arunachal Pradesh, 8 in Chhattisgarh and 8 in MP. The Committee was informed that a
proposal involving annual expenditure of Rs. 492.67 lakhs and non-recurring one time expenditure of Rs. 123 lakhs for
creation of 123x3 posts for these Kendras has been submitted to Ministry of Finance.  The Committee would like to
remind the Ministry on the controversies arose during its last selection process of Youth Coordinators.  The
confusion and uncertainity over the last recruitment process is still not over. The Committee feels that the court cases
pertaining to last recruitment of Youth Coordinators need to be pursued vigorously for early settlement. The Ministry,
needs to be equally cautious about its fresh proposal of recruitment with the Finance Ministry so that the process of
selection remains transparent and does not raise any doubts. The Committee would appreciate if a status report on the
issue is submitted for its consideration.                                    
 (Para 4.10)
                        The Committee has been emphasizing in its earlier Reports the need for strengthening the monitoring
mechanism of NYKS by association of elected representatives.  The Committee understands that instructions have been
issued to the District Youth Coordinators to involve M.Ps, MLAs and other public representatives in the activities of
NYKS.  District Youth Coordinators are also supposed to send the minutes of the meetings of the District Advisory
Committee for Youth Programmes to respective MPs/MLAs.    The Committee would like to have an idea about the
level of compliance of these instructions by the District Youth Coordinators.           (Para 4.11)
V.        NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME
                        An allocation of Rs. 31.50 crores has been made for NSS under plan in 2006-2007 against a provision of
Rs. 26.10 crores last year. The allocation this year has been kept on higher side due to the increase in the enrolment of
students in various universities and colleges.  Also there is a proposal to introduce National Service Scheme from IXth
class onwards. The Committee would like the Ministry to consider introduction of NSS from class IX itself in the
light of noble objectives of the scheme.
                       (Para 5.2)
                        The Committee understands that there is a need to deploy more number of National Service Volunteers
who act as link between the Kendra and village based Rural Youth Clubs.  The Committee strongly feels that it is high
time for acknowledging the good work being done by NSS volunteers. Their efforts need to be encouraged and
commensurated with good incentives. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the incentive given to NSS
volunteers should be enhanced and brought at par with the incentives provided to the NCC cadets so that they perform
their duties with greater zest and vigour.                                                                         (Para 5.4)
                        The role of State Liaison Cells is conceived as the fountainhead for ensuring timely release of grants,
monitoring and liaison with the universities and +2 level councils.  Non-existence of such Liaison Cells in some States
itself indicates the plight of NSS activities. Perhaps the Ministry has failed to persuade the States/UTs in setting up such
an important functionary of the scheme. The Committee would like the Ministry to impress upon the States the
importance of the Liaisoning Cells and take up the matter at the highest level of those States not having set up these
cells so far. (Para 5.6)
                        The Committee is of the view that the Ministry can no longer afford to be a mere spectator on the
sensitive issues involving release of finances from the national exchequer. There is an urgent need to review the
accounting procedure under NSS so that the defaulting States adopt proper fiscal disciplines.                          (Para 5.8)
VI.       NATIONAL DISCIPLINE SCHEME
                        The Committee regrets that repeated reminders from the Department to some States have not evinced any

176th Report of Committee on Human Resource Development
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/176threport%20.htm[01-07-2016 15:28:47]
response and the issue of committed liabilities remains un-resolved for years together. The Committee feels that this
situation of uncertainty should come to a halt. A time has come when the Ministry should fix a final deadline for such
States to avoid this never-ending chaotic scenario. The Ministry should settle the issue once for all after paying the
liabilities to those States who have furnished the information. The States who do not respond may have to forgo their
claims. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would plan the whole process to ensure settlement of committed
liabilities within this financial year itself. The Committee would also like the Ministry to appeal to the States to avail
this opportunity and expedite their claims without further loss of time.                  (Para 6.4)
VII.     YOUTH HOSTELS
The Committee notes that the allocations have not been utilised optimally. Main areas of concern have
been the inordinate delay in construction process of Youth Hostels.  The status of 18 Youth Hostels under construction
indicate shocking revelations. There are Youth Hostels which were approved long back in 1986 and even instalments of
central funds for construction were released. For instance an instalment of Rs.15 lakhs was released in March 1989 in
respect of a Youth Hostel in Himachal Pradesh and the State Govt. has not even handed over the developed plot of land
for construction of the project.  Construction of Youth Hostel in Allahabad was approved in principle in April 1988, and
State Government identified the land in 1998.  First instalment of central funds amounting to Rs. 20.00 lakhs was
released in March 1990 and the construction is yet to be completed.  Position with regard to the remaining Youth
Hostels is more or less the same.  The Committee notes that even pursuing the issue with the concerned State Chief
Secretaries has not brought any noticeable impact.  The Committee observes that with the passage of time, estimates for
construction have kept on increasing steadily, leading to criminal wastage of Government funds. (Para 7.2)
The Committee recommends that specific action needs to be initiated to remedy the problem. Stringent
action is required to be taken in respect of some places which ultimately will have its impact in other places also. Even
the extreme step for recovery of the instalment to central pool may be contemplated in such cases where the
construction work has not started even 3 years after the release of instalments(s). The Committee would like to have a
status note on the utilisation of instalments released for all such incomplete projects.                             (Para 7.3)
VIII.  PROMOTION OF YOUTH ACTIVITIES AND TRAINING
The Committee apprehends that the above pendency must have increased further in view of an
expenditure of Rs. 9.66 crores being incurred under this scheme during 2004-05.  The Committee has been given to
understand that action has been taken to stop further grants to such organizations.   The Committee would like to have
the feedback  from those NGOs who have not been released further grant due to their past performance.
                                     (Para 8.3)
IX.       NATIONAL INTEGRATION PROGRAMME
 
                        The Scheme provides the framework for greater exchange and understanding among the youth belonging
to different regions of the country.  The two components of this scheme are National Integration Camp and Inter State
Youth Exchange Programme administered by NGOs and other agencies.   The Committee notes that achievement level
for both physical and financial targets has been by and large satisfactory.    Additional funds are also being  provided 
due to the tremendous response being received from the implementing agencies.   During 2005-06, plan allocation of
Rs. 4.95 crore was enhanced to Rs. 5.50 crore and actual expenditure reported upto 20
th March 2006 is Rs. 5.11 crore. 
The Committee notes that provision of Rs. 10.00 crore has been made for the scheme for 2006-07. The Committee’s
attention however, has been drawn by the status of pendency of utilization certificates spread over different States under
this programme.   As many as 27 UCs, 110 UCs and 120 UCs for 2002-03, 2003-04 and 2004-05 respectively are yet to
be received from implementing agencies.   These are the figures in respect of NGOs.  Status of other implementing
agencies is not known to the Committee. The Committee strongly feels that urgent action is required to be taken in this
matter. Under no circumstances, defaulter NGOs should be provided further assistance.               (Para 9.1)
X.  MISCELLANEOUS
                   The Committee would like to reiterate its earlier recommendation that any new scheme should be
launched only after the completion of all the preliminary formalities.                                            (Para 10.2)
XI.       SPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA (SAI)
                        The Committee is not convinced with the Ministry’s excuse for inadequate resources, when the allocation

176th Report of Committee on Human Resource Development
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/176threport%20.htm[01-07-2016 15:28:47]
so received remain underutilised. Unfortunately the Ministry has not shared the utilization figures for the previous year
with the Committee.  Needless to say, the trend of unspent balances with SAI is quite disappointing a fact to suggest
serious steps for restructuring of SAI to make it a more effective and professional body.                                                 
(Para 11.3)
                        The Committee is dismayed to note that after conversion of NSTC Scheme from residential to day
boarding, the intake of children in the scheme in most of the adopted regular schools both in individual as well as team
event is quite less. The Committee is not sure whether proper consultations with all the stakeholders has taken place
before finally converting the mode of scheme. The Committee is also not inclined to agree with Ministry’s argument
that intake of children in the Navodaya Vidyalayas is far from satisfactory due to non-availability of talented children. 
Most of the NVs are located in the rural areas and it would be the weakness of Govternment’s Rural Sports Programme
in case they fail to tap rural talent.  The Committee, however, appreciates the role of ABSCs in providing job
opportunities to those excelling in performance after attaining the age of 17 ½ years in the Indian Army. The Committee
would like the Ministry to expand the coverage of the scheme in all States in view of its utility.           (Para 11.4)
                        The Committee is unhappy with the low expenditure on traditional/indigenous games during the last
three years. This fact is reflected in the drastic reduction of funds to these federations over the years. The Committee
feels that there are no clear-cut guidelines to either State Governments or SAI centres about the promotion of indigenous
games. The appraisal of these games is also not possible as no State-wise grant is released for the purpose. The
continuous decline in allocation over the years itself indicates reluctance of Government towards these disciplines. The
Committee is surprised on Ministry’s assertion that they are not short of funds. In fact, if it is so the Ministry should not
have any problem in persuading the federations to avail optimum funds from the Government for promotion of
indigenous games.                              (Para 11.6)
                        The Committee has been concerned about poor level of achievement in Olympics inspite of good
performance at Asian and Commonwealth Games. The representatives of the Ministry clarified  that pre-qualification
standards in Olympic Games are very tough.  To overcome the problem, the numbers of trainees are proposed to be
increased from 10,000 to 15,000 in SAI training centers.  Efforts are also on to strengthen the rural sports.  At Panchayat
level efforts are initiated so that the children from rural areas could also be benefited and get encouragement to join
sports.  It would be helpful in upgrading the skills of the talented, which is in abundant in rural areas.  He assured that
by adopting such measures more medals could be achieved in 2010 and 2014
Games.                                                                                      (Para 11.7)
                        The Committee understands that there are 5 main SAI centers in the country.  However, of these centres
i.e. NERC, Imphal still continues to function as a sub-centre as there is no full-fledged Director. The Committee is
surprised at such peculiar status of the centre. The Committee is of the view that this centre would work better if it is
declared as a full-fledged centre with adequate manpower and infrastructure.                                                        (Para
11.8)
                        The Committee is aware that there is no dearth of sporting talent in the country. Proper hunting/searching
and nurturing of the talent is required. Talent is in abundance in schools and educational institutions.  States are
allocated funds for development of sports.  But educational institutions do not have physical instructors.  The
Committee feels that the talent search process is not able to get the reach it requires. People remain in dark about such
exercise. Present system of selection has not yielded the desired results and the talent has still remained unspotted.
The Central Government, State Government and the sport authorities should, therefore, give adequate publicity
through advertisement to such events.         (Para 11.9)
XII.     PROMOTION OF SPORTS AMONG DISABLED
                        Only a token provision was made for the scheme in 2003-04, 2004-05 and 2005-06 as the scheme had not
been formulated.   The Committee has been given to understand that the scheme is likely to be included in the umbrella
scheme related to events.   Accordingly, no provision has been made in 2006-07.  The Committee takes strong
exception to this kind of approach.   This clearly indicates that the Ministry is not serious about the necessity of
providing any kind of incentives to the disadvantaged segment of our
society.                                                                        (Para 12.1)
XIII.   SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE SCHEME

176th Report of Committee on Human Resource Development
